jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer (COO)**
Unity Care Group**Department:** Administration  

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer (CEO)  

**FLSA Status:** Exempt**Salary Range:** $150,000 \- $175,000 **Position Summary**
Unity Care Group is seeking a strategic, mission\-driven, and operationally strong Chief Operating Officer (COO) to provide executive leadership and oversight across the agency’s programs, operations, and administrative functions. Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO will serve as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team and help advance Unity Care’s integrated model of Housing, Education, Employment, Well\-Being, and Unconditional Care.
The COO will oversee day\-to\-day agency operations, strengthen organizational systems, ensure operational excellence, support financial sustainability, and help drive strategic growth across behavioral health, housing, foster care, and supportive services programs throughout the Bay Area.
The ideal candidate is a collaborative and emotionally intelligent leader with deep experience in healthcare, behavioral health, social services, or nonprofit operations who can build high\-performing teams, improve organizational accountability, and lead complex multi\-program environments with integrity, transparency, and a servant leadership philosophy. **Key Responsibilities** **Executive \& Operational Leadership*** Provide day\-to\-day leadership, oversight, and management of agency programs and administrative operations.
* Execute the agency’s strategic plan and ensure alignment with organizational goals, contractual outcomes, and service excellence.
* Develop and strengthen operational systems, workflows, policies, and infrastructure to improve organizational efficiency, accountability, scalability, and communication.
* Monitor performance metrics, KPIs, program outcomes, and operational effectiveness to support data\-driven decision\-making.
* Ensure compliance with county, state, federal, licensing, Medi\-Cal, and contractual requirements.
* Support operational integration across behavioral health, housing, education, employment, and supportive services programs.

 **Financial \& Contract Oversight*** Oversee operational budgets, contract performance, and fiscal accountability in partnership with Finance leadership.
* Monitor service utilization, billing, staffing, and program performance to maximize revenue and operational sustainability.
* Support development and implementation of diversified funding and growth strategies.
* Assist in identifying and pursuing new contracts, grant, and partnership opportunities.

 **Program \& Organizational Development*** Support expansion and enhancement of behavioral health, housing, foster care, workforce development, and youth services programs.
* Ensure culturally responsive, trauma\-informed, and evidence\-based practices are embedded throughout service delivery.
* Improve cross\-functional collaboration and reduce organizational silos across departments and counties served.
* Support organizational change management, continuous quality improvement, and innovation initiatives.

 **Leadership \& Culture*** Foster a collaborative, strengths\-based, and servant leadership culture focused on accountability, transparency, innovation, and professional growth.
* Coach and develop program and administrative leaders while establishing clear performance expectations.
* Promote staff wellness, psychological safety, inclusion, and employee engagement.
* Lead with emotional intelligence, humility, professionalism, and integrity.

 **Executive Partnership \& External Relations*** Serve as a strategic operational partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
* Represent Unity Care at county, state, community, and public meetings as delegated by the CEO.
* Support Board of Directors reporting, strategic planning, and organizational initiatives.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with county partners, healthcare systems, foundations, community organizations, and stakeholders.

 **Qualifications****Education \& Experience*** Master’s degree in business administration, Public Administration, Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Social Work, or related field preferred. Equivalent executive leadership experience will be considered.
* Minimum 10 years of senior leadership experience in nonprofit, behavioral health, healthcare, foster care, housing, or social services organizations.
* Demonstrated success managing complex multi\-program operations and multi\-million\-dollar budgets.
* Experience overseeing contracts, compliance, operational systems, and organizational growth initiatives.
* Strong understanding of behavioral health, Medi\-Cal, housing, and community\-based service systems preferred.
* Proven ability to lead high\-performing teams and drive organizational improvement in dynamic environments.

 **Leadership Competencies*** Strategic and solutions\-oriented thinker
* Strong operational and organizational leadership
* Collaborative and relationship\-centered
* High emotional intelligence and resilience
* Transparent communicator with strong follow\-through
* Mission\-driven with commitment to equity and underserved communities
* Servant leader committed to developing people and strengthening culture

 **About Unity Care Group**
Unity Care Group is dedicated to empowering youth and families through compassionate, culturally responsive services that create healing, stability, and opportunity. The COO will play a critical role in strengthening operations, supporting sustainable growth, and advancing the organization’s mission and long\-term impact throughout the communities we serve.

jobs.title: J.P. Morgan Wealth Management - Executive Director, Advanced Planner Wealth Advisor - San Francisco and San Jose, CA
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Wealth Planning \& Advice is a group of experts in trusts \& estates, tax planning, financial planning and planning in related areas for individuals and their entities (operating businesses, private foundations, etc.). Our role is to work with advisors and their clients to educate them about wealth planning opportunities both simple (e.g., asset titling, beneficiary designations) and complex (e.g., GRATs, split\-interest trusts). We provide intellectual capital to clients across the wealth continuum and will work one\-on\-one with clients in appropriate circumstances. Familiarity with the taxation of entities and of estates and trusts is also useful but not required. Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds) will also be a plus.


As the Executive Director, Wealth Planner within J.P. Morgan Wealth Management, you will leverage your deep understanding of tax and trust \& estate laws to communicate complex information in a simple, non\-technical manner to both clients and advisors, as well as field leadership. You will adopt a goal\-oriented approach when engaging with clients, which involves familiarizing yourself with the various investment, banking, and lending products and platforms available to our advisors across J.P. Morgan Wealth Management. This knowledge will enable you to identify issues and opportunities for client engagement. Additionally, you will collaborate with field management to develop regional strategies and provide guidance on their execution. A natural curiosity for people, planning, and the wealth management industry, along with independent initiative and responsiveness, are essential qualities for success in this role.


**Job Responsibilities:**


* Work with divisional leadership and WP\&A leadership to develop and present content across different wealth management topics.
* Serve as a resource to the JPMWM field in the areas of both simple and sophisticated tax and trust \& estate planning strategies as well as in concentrated position management, corporate executive services, and pre\-liquidity transaction planning.
* Partner with field leadership and Practice Management to integrate estate and tax planning concepts into goals\-based advice.
* Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of both federal and state tax laws relating to our areas of focus.
* Promote J.P. Morgan's knowledge and sophistication to outside centers of influence, primarily accountants and attorneys.
* Work with Advisors to develop business opportunities with new and existing clients.
* Provide unbiased comprehensive and customized wealth planning advice to clients and prospective clients.
* Work with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies.
* Actively participate in team discussions to proactively propose planning ideas and industry trends that can be shared with the field.
* Travel to local and out of state branches, as needed.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* 4\-year college degree and either J.D, LLB, CPA or CFP
* 7 plus years of practice as a trusts \& estates lawyer, tax advisor, or financial planner
* Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds.
* Must be comfortable working with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies; familiarity with financial planning, investments, and corporate executive issues.
* Ability to drive business results with broad background in trust and estate planning issues.
* A strong self\-motivated individual who can work closely with Advisors without daily contact with a direct manager.
* Strong presentation skills in one\-on\-one and group meetings
* Experience and ability in understanding clients' financial situations and personal circumstances
* Must be able to coach colleagues, Financial Advisors and clients (very strong partnership skills)
* Individual with high ethical standards who never sacrifices integrity and works in the clients' best interest

**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* Series 7 \& 66 required (may be fulfilled within 4 months of assuming role)
* Familiarity with financial planning, investments, corporate executive issues and concentrated stock management is a plus
* 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds, and concentrated stock management is a plus
* Experience with financial planning software a plus

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT:


This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase's review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.


**ABOUT US**  

  

  

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.


We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission\-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions.

jobs.title: Science & Policy Director
jobs.description:
**About the Organization**


Heal the Bay is the most recognized environmental nonprofit group in LA for a reason: we have been keeping Southern California's coastal waters and watersheds safe, healthy, and clean for people and marine life since 1985\. Using education, science, advocacy, and community action, we raise awareness and make progress with practical solutions to often complex problems. We conduct hundreds of beach and community cleanups each year, informing people about the root causes of pollution along the shorelines and in their neighborhoods. We advocate for strict water quality regulations that protect the health of both humans and the animals that call local creeks, rivers, and the Santa Monica Bay home. We operate the award\-winning Heal the Bay Aquarium at the Santa Monica Pier, inspiring visitors to become stewards for the region’s most important natural resource: clean water. We also educate and inspire the next generation of environmental stewards, with more than 10,000 students joining us each year for school field trips, science\-based classroom presentations, and events. Learn more about us at www.healthebay.org/our\-impact

**About the Role**


The Science \& Policy Director is a key leadership role at Heal the Bay, responsible for advancing our mission of making coastal waters and watersheds in Greater Los Angeles safe, healthy, and clean.


Reporting to the CEO, the Director manages a team of scientists and policy experts to drive strategic goals, with a focus on inland and coastal water quality, biodiversity, climate change and environmental justice. Specifically, Heal the Bay’s current strategic science and policy priorities include:

* **Clean Water \& Public Health** – Protecting the health of people and coastal waters by reducing urban runoff, stormwater, wastewater, nutrients, and other sources of pollution; advancing stormwater capture and watershed solutions; providing trusted water\-quality information; and serving as a watchdog for water\-quality regulations and NPDES permits.
* **Marine Ecosystem Protection \& Restoration** – Protecting and restoring healthy marine ecosystems and biodiversity through science, policy, MPAs, responsible resource management, and applied conservation and restorative aquaculture. Oversee Heal the Bay’s conservation and restorative aquaculture work at the Aquarium/Research \& Discovery Center, ensuring projects are scientifically rigorous, mission\-aligned, and connected to broader restoration and policy priorities.
* **Climate \& Coastal Resilience** – Integrating climate change into Heal the Bay’s science and policy priorities and advancing solutions that strengthen the resilience of coastal and watershed ecosystems and Greater Los Angeles communities.
* **Pollution Prevention** – Reducing plastics, DDT and other legacy contaminants, and emerging and industrial pollutants through science\-based policy, advocacy, source reduction, and systems change.
* **Science\-Based Response to Emerging \& Acute Threats** – Helping Heal the Bay identify and respond appropriately to emerging or acute threats to coastal ecosystems and public health, including sewage releases, oil spills, wildfires, and other significant pollution events.


Key responsibilities include working with the CEO to develop the overall strategic vision for achieving Heal the Bay’s science and policy goals. Independently, the Director is responsible for developing advocacy campaigns, overseeing research and regulatory analyses, and representing Heal the Bay in public forums. The Director also manages relationships with policymakers in Los Angeles and Sacramento and collaborates with external partners.


Candidates should have a strong background in environmental policy and science, with expertise in one or more of the following areas: water quality, ocean and coastal policy, climate change and its impacts on Los Angeles’ coastline, and environmental justice. The ideal candidate will have at least five years of experience leading a team.


Heal the Bay offers a dynamic, mission\-driven environment where science, education, community action, and advocacy are at the core of our work.

**Expectations \& Responsibilities**

* **Lead science, policy, and advocacy efforts** on water quality and coastal resources, in alignment with Heal the Bay’s strategic goals.
	+ **Cultivate and maintain partnerships** with government agencies, decision\-makers, advocacy groups, and environmental stakeholders.
	+ **Track and analyze** policies, regulations, and legislation at regional and state levels.
	+ **Develop, review, and provide feedback** on scientific, technical, and regulatory documents.
	+ **Develop and lead campaigns** to pass legislation and regulations and implement programs that help Heal the Bay achieve our mission.
* **Manage department staff;** lead, mentor, and develop a team of scientists and policy experts, fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment.
* **Collaborate with department directors** on inter\-departmental projects that integrate, and Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusivity (JEDI) principles into Heal the Bay’s overall strategy.
* **Manage relationships with funders and help identify new funding sources**, oversee grants and budgets, and manage the department's budget.
* **Engage Heal the Bay’s Board of Directors**, providing updates on science and policy issues and offering guidance on policy decisions that align with the organization's mission.

**Experience \& Skills**

* **Deep commitment to Heal the Bay’s mission** and the protection of environmental health in Southern California.
* **Extensive experience in environmental science, policy, or law**, with 10\+ years in environmental policy, water management, coastal/ocean management, or related fields.
* **Relationships with policymakers** in Los Angeles and Sacramento.
* **Advanced degree** demonstrating expertise in environmental disciplines.

jobs.description:
**Aviva Family and Children's Services Mission Statement**


Creating safe, supportive spaces where children, youth and families can heal, build resilience, and experience belonging.

**Job Summary**


The Program Director is responsible for the day\-to\-day clinical and administrative operations of an assigned Substance Use Disorder (SUD) program. The Program Director ensures that the treatment provided is consistent with Aviva's philosophy and meets the current standards for quality of care, medical necessity, and outcome measurements as defined by the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health, Department of Public Health Substance Abuse Prevention and Control (SAPC), and other applicable regulatory and accrediting bodies.


The Program Director provides direct supervision to Clinical Supervisor(s), Therapists, Alcohol and Other Drug Counselors, Supervisors, and other program staff as assigned, and is accountable for quality improvement, staff development, contract compliance, and the fiscal viability of the program. The Program Director coordinates and collaborates with other Aviva programs, community organizations, and regulatory agencies to promote and strengthen the SUD program.


The Program Director is an energetic self\-starter who can function comfortably in a team environment or independently and relates well to co\-workers and County representatives. This position requires flexibility and the ability to manage time and multiple tasks with little supervision. The individual in this position must be able to assume a wide range of responsibilities, provide timely responses to requests and deadlines, and work well under pressure.

jobs.title: Executive Director, News & Media Relations
jobs.description:
The Executive Director, News \& Media Relations is a senior leader within UCSF's Office of Communications and serves as the institution's principal strategist for enterprise media relations and public affairs. Reporting to the Vice Chancellor, Communications, this position develops and leads integrated external communications strategies for UCSF. The role works in partnership with communications and institutional leaders across the enterprise to protect and strengthen UCSF's reputation as one of the world's leading academic health systems and biomedical research institutions. It also advances institutional priorities across research, education, patient care, and public service.
  

  

The Executive Director provides strategic communications counsel to executive leadership and ensures a coordinated, enterprise\-wide approach to external communications.
  

  

**Primary Responsibilities**  

  

The Executive Director is responsible for leading UCSF's external communications strategy through the Public Affairs function by:


* Developing and executing integrated external communications strategies that advance institutional priorities and strengthen UCSF's reputation through media relations, public affairs, and executive visibility.
* Serving as the senior strategic advisor to executive leadership on media relations and public affairs for the UCSF enterprise.
* Directing enterprise\-wide media relations, including oversight of earned and owned media strategies, media engagement, and rapid response communications.
* Leading and developing a high\-performing Public Affairs team through coaching, mentorship, talent development, and a culture of innovation, accountability, and excellence.
* Driving innovation in storytelling by leveraging emerging communications technologies, evolving media platforms, analytics, and audience insights to increase communications effectiveness and institutional impact.

***WHY CHOOSE US?***  

Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional, yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.  



  

**Where Your Career is a Force for Good!**

  

The American Red Cross is currently seeking t **he Regional CEO for the Greater New York Region** . **Headquartered in New York City,** the Greater New York Region serves more than 12 million people in New York City, Long Island, Rockland and Westchester Counties, and Greenwich, Connecticut, and is the highest\-profile Region in the Red Cross network.

The Regional CEO leads a team of paid and volunteer staff to prevent and alleviate human suffering in the face of emergencies and support resilient communities throughout the Region by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors. Regional Board and Advisory Board recruitment.

The New York City Taxi \& Limousine Commission (TLC) oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly one million riders every single day, which is the equivalent of the entire transit system of a medium sized city. The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) is the agency responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for\-hire vehicle industry. With 180,000 licensed drivers and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our city’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for\-hire vehicle sector. TLC continues to be on the front lines of a rapidly changing mobility landscape and our innovative efforts\-whether requiring minimum pay for app drivers, ensuring wheelchair accessible service, making our licensed fleet more environmentally sustainable, working to eliminate traffic fatalities, or preventing discriminatory service\-often serve as a model for other cities.
  

  

We are seeking a strategic, imaginative, politically savvy Chief Communications Officer (CCO) to help shape and amplify this new chapter of TLC, focused on three major strategic priorities: driver and passenger dignity, corporate accountability, and a transportation system that works together. This is a rare opportunity to lead communications for one of the most visible, impactful, and culturally resonant public agencies in New York City.
  

  

The CCO will report to the Commissioner and will serve as TLC’s on\-the\-record Communications Director, the primary voice of the agency across traditional media, social platforms, public events, and crisis communications. The Chief Communications Officer oversees a small team working closely with the Commissioner’s Office, the Office of Community Affairs, and policy and operations teams to ensure communications is not an afterthought but a driver of trust, transparency, and meaningful engagement.
  

  

The CCO will lead the charge on four core goals:

jobs.title: Director of Operations and Facilities
jobs.description:
Brooklyn Defender Services (BDS) seeks a Director of Operations and Facilities.


BDS is a public defense office representing low\-income New Yorkers in criminal, family, immigration, and civil legal matters. BDS has 750\+ employees with multiple locations in Brooklyn and Queens in New York City. Our work with clients is focused on the intersection of the legal systems that disproportionately impact Black and Brown people living below the poverty level in Brooklyn and Queens.


BDS represents thousands of people each year who have diverse, complex, and multi\-faceted legal needs. In addition to a zealous legal defense, our interdisciplinary teams of attorneys, social workers and advocates provide a wide range of legal and advocacy services, including in the areas of housing, public benefits, education, and employment. BDS staff work collaboratively and across disciplines to deliver high\-quality legal services that serve the people we represent, their families and communities.


The Director of Operations and Facilities is responsible for the strategic planning, day\-to\-day operations, and continuous improvement of all facilities\-related functions across the organization. This role ensures that physical spaces are safe, functional, compliant, and aligned with organizational needs, while delivering a high\-quality workplace infrastructure for staff and visitors.


The role combines operational leadership, facilities planning, vendor management and cross\-functional collaboration to maintain and enhance workplace infrastructure.

**Responsibilities**

* Oversee all facilities operations.
* Supervise Operations Staff.
* Prepare and keep up on budget for facilities and operational needs.
* Approve invoices, track spending trends, and implement cost\-control strategies.
* Lead RFP processes, contract negotiations, and performance evaluations for vendors related to facilities and operations.
* Ensure all vendors meet service level agreements, compliance standards, and cost expectations.
* Emergency preparedness.
* Respond to urgent issues and coordinate rapid resolution of facility\-related incidents.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer and other leadership to align facilities strategy with organizational growth and programmatic needs.
* Project management of facilities and operational issues as they arise.
* At the current time, BDS is renovating a new space that is on track to be completed in late 2027\-2028\. The Director of Operations and Facilities will be involved in tracking progress and implementing the new space when it comes online.

**Qualifications**

* 7–10\+ years of facilities or operations management experience.
* Demonstrated experience managing multi\-site facilities.
* Knowledge of building systems, safety regulations, and compliance requirements.
* Proven ability to manage budgets and drive cost efficiencies.
* Experience in nonprofit, legal services, or mission\-driven organizations preferred.
* Prior experience with a large renovation a plus.

**Key Competencies**

* Strategic and operational leadership.
* Strong project management skills.
* Problem\-solving and decision\-making under pressure.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management.
* Attention to detail with a service\-oriented mindset.
* Ability to balance long\-term planning with day\-to\-day operational demands.

**Position Information**


This is a full\-time, exempt, salaried position. The normal schedule is Monday to Friday 9am\-5pm. The position is based at BDS’s offices in Brooklyn and Queens, with regular travel between office locations as needed. The role also may require after\-hours availability for emergencies or major facilities projects.


BDS determines salary on a pay scale based on education and experience. For this position there is a salary range of $125,000\-$150,000\. For someone with extensive experience, it is possible BDS would consider additional salary. BDS offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance and a 403(b)\-retirement plan. To support work/life balance and family\-friendly policies, BDS has generous vacation, sick, holiday, family, and medical leave policies.

**Application Instructions**


Click “Apply Now” to submit a cover letter and resume.


Please submit your application by**October 30, 2026\.**

*Brooklyn Defender Services is a proud equal opportunity employer committed to celebrating diversity and maintaining an equitable and inclusive work environment. We strongly encourage candidates of all identities, expressions, orientations, disabilities, and experiences to apply. If you require an accommodation due to a disability or another reason, please contact the Managing Director of Human Resources, Christina Wallace, at* *cwallace @ bds.org**.*

**Title:** Executive Director **Reports to:** Board of Directors **Location:** Hays, Kansas (on\-site) **FLSA status:** Exempt, full\-time

About Grow Hays

Grow Hays, Inc., a 501(c)(3\) not\-for\-profit organization, is the lead economic development organization for Hays and Ellis County, Kansas. It works to attract new business investment, help existing employers grow, and strengthen the workforce, housing, and infrastructure that growth depends on. Its funding partners include Ellis County, the City of Hays, the City of Ellis, the City of Victoria, and numerous private sector organizations.

Ellis County is a regional hub for northwest Kansas, with anchors in health care, higher education, energy, agriculture, retail, and transportation along I\-70\. Grow Hays partners closely with the City of Hays, Ellis County, Fort Hays State University, Fort Hays Technical College, the Hays Area Chamber of Commerce, Visit Hays, The Bricks, Hays Medical Center, Midwest Energy, and state partners including the Kansas Department of Commerce.

Grow Hays has been the driving force behind the construction of the Grow Hays MicroFactory, the Bob \& Pat Schmidt Community Center, and The Tallgrass and The Grove housing developments. It has also originated more than $3 million in small business loans.

Position Summary

The Executive Director is the chief executive and primary spokesperson for Grow Hays, reporting to the Board of Directors. This is a working executive role: the Director sets strategy and also personally manages business prospects, incentive negotiations, and development projects.

The Director is the main liaison between the Board, the City of Hays, Ellis County, business leaders, education partners, and state and regional agencies. The Director supervises a staff of three (four full\-time equivalent positions in total, including the Director) and is accountable for the organization's budget, programs, and results.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Strategy and Board Relations

* Develop and carry out a countywide economic development strategy with the Board, and update it regularly.
* Advise the Board on policy, priorities, and emerging opportunities; prepare board meeting materials and reports.
* Track and report performance metrics such as jobs created, capital investment, wages, and tax base growth.

Business Attraction

* Serve as the primary contact for the Kansas Department of Commerce, site selectors, and companies considering Ellis County.
* Respond to requests for information and proposals, host site visits, and manage prospects from first contact through location decision.
* Maintain an inventory of available sites and buildings, public and private, and supporting community data.
* Market Ellis County through digital channels, trade shows, and regional and state marketing partnerships.

Business Retention and Expansion

* Run a regular visitation program with existing employers to learn their needs and head off risks of closure or relocation.
* Connect businesses to financing, workforce training, and state and federal programs.
* Support entrepreneurs and small businesses in coordination with the Chamber, The Bricks, and the Small Business Development Center.

Incentives, Finance, and Projects

* Structure and negotiate incentive packages using Kansas tools such as IRBs, tax abatements, TIF, CIDs, STAR bonds, HOME and Moderate Income Housing programs, and revolving loan funds.
* Work with the City and County on local incentive policies and performance\-based agreements, and monitor compliance.
* Lead or support site, infrastructure, and housing development projects from concept to completion.
* Identify, write, and manage grants.

Workforce and Housing

* Identify employer workforce needs and work with Fort Hays State University, Fort Hays Technical College, USD 489, and KANSASWORKS on training and talent pipelines.
* Support housing development to meet workforce demand.

Partnerships and Advocacy

* Build strong working relationships with elected officials, the City Manager, County Administrator, and regional partners.
* Represent Grow Hays in the community, the media, and state and regional organizations such as the Kansas Economic Development Alliance.
* Handle confidential business information with discretion.

Operations and Finance

* Prepare and manage the annual budget; oversee financial reporting, audits, and funding agreements.
* Lead private investor and public funding campaigns.
* Hire, supervise, and develop staff and manage contractors.

*Other duties as assigned. This list illustrates the work and is not exhaustive.*

Qualifications

Required

* Bachelor's degree in economics, business, public administration, planning, finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 3\+ years of experience in economic development, commercial real estate, business finance, or a related field, including at least 2 years supervising staff or managing major projects.
* Proven success managing projects involving multiple public and private partners.
* Strong public speaking, writing, negotiation, and relationship\-building skills.
* Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly.

Preferred

* Certified Economic Developer (CEcD) designation from IEDC, or progress toward it.
* Working knowledge of Kansas incentive and finance tools (IRBs, TIF, CIDs, STAR bonds, HOME, abatements, revolving loan funds).
* Experience in a rural or micropolitan community.
* Experience working for or with a nonprofit board.
* Grant writing and grant management experience.

Key Competencies

* Strategic thinking with hands\-on execution.
* Financial literacy: budgets, pro formas, and incentive analysis.
* Discretion with confidential information.
* Collaborative, consensus\-building style with elected officials and business leaders.
* Comfort with CRM, data tools, and social media for marketing.

**Chief Operating Officer (COO)**
=================================


**Annapolis Area Christian School (AACS)**  

**Annapolis, Maryland Area**


**About Annapolis Area Christian School**
-----------------------------------------


Annapolis Area Christian School (AACS) is a Christ\-centered educational community committed to engaging students in an education of excellence that prepares them to serve God in all areas of life.


AACS is seeking an experienced, mission\-driven leader to serve as its **Chief Operating Officer (COO)**. This individual will play a critical leadership role in ensuring that the school's people, resources, facilities, and operational systems effectively support its educational mission and long\-term vision.


The COO will combine strong business and operational leadership with a genuine commitment to Christian education. Working closely with the Head of School, accounting and business functions, and the senior leadership team, the COO will help translate the school's strategic priorities into effective, sustainable operations.


**Position Summary**
--------------------


The Chief Operating Officer is responsible for leading and coordinating AACS's major business and operational functions. The COO will bring organizational discipline, financial stewardship, strategic thinking, and a service\-oriented approach to the school's operations.


This is a senior leadership position requiring someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution—developing long\-term plans while ensuring that the school's day\-to\-day operations are effective, accountable, and aligned with its mission.


A significant emphasis of the position will be **financial planning and analysis (FP\&A)**. The COO will move AACS beyond traditional budgeting and financial reporting toward a more forward\-looking financial management model that uses forecasting, scenario modeling, data analysis, and key performance indicators to inform strategic decisions and strengthen the school's long\-term financial sustainability.


The successful candidate will be a collaborative leader who builds trust, develops strong teams, improves systems, manages resources wisely, and approaches leadership as an opportunity for Christian service and stewardship.


**Christian Faith \& Mission Alignment**
----------------------------------------


Because AACS is a Christian school, the COO must demonstrate a personal commitment to Jesus Christ, be active in a local Christian church, and wholeheartedly align with the school's Christian mission, beliefs, and values.


The COO should view leadership and stewardship as forms of service and should model integrity, humility, wisdom, and Christ\-centered leadership in interactions with employees, students, families, and the broader AACS community.


**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------


### **Strategic \& Organizational Leadership**


 Partner with the Head of School, business office team, and senior leadership team to advance AACS's mission, strategic plan, and institutional priorities.


 Translate strategic objectives into actionable operational and financial plans.


 Develop systems, processes, and accountability structures that enable the school to operate effectively and sustainably.


 Identify organizational risks and opportunities and provide thoughtful recommendations to school leadership.


 Foster a culture of collaboration, excellence, stewardship, accountability, and continuous improvement.


### **Financial Planning \& Analysis (FP\&A)**

* Lead AACS's financial planning and analysis function, ensuring that financial information is used proactively to inform strategic, operational, and capital decisions.
* Develop and maintain multi\-year financial models that integrate enrollment, tuition and financial aid, compensation and benefits, staffing, facilities, debt, capital investment, and other key drivers of the school's financial model.
* Build annual and long\-range financial forecasts and regularly update projections based on actual performance, enrollment trends, and changing organizational assumptions.
* Conduct budget\-to\-actual and forecast\-to\-actual variance analysis, identifying significant trends and providing leadership with clear explanations and recommended actions.
* Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to evaluate significant strategic decisions, including enrollment changes, tuition strategies, staffing models, compensation investments, capital projects, debt management, and program expansion or contraction.
* Partner with academic and operational leaders to understand the financial implications of their programs, staffing decisions, and strategic priorities.
* Develop meaningful financial and operational KPIs and dashboards that provide the Head of School and senior leadership with timely insight into organizational performance.
* Evaluate the financial sustainability and return on investment of existing and proposed programs and initiatives while recognizing that mission impact, rather than financial return alone, is central to decision\-making in a Christian school.
* Provide forward\-looking analysis of cash flow, liquidity, reserves, debt capacity, and capital requirements to support responsible long\-term financial stewardship.
* Identify emerging financial risks and opportunities early and develop actionable recommendations for the Head of School and senior leadership.
* Translate complex financial data into clear, actionable information for leaders who may not have financial backgrounds.
* Strengthen a culture in which financial planning is integrated with strategic planning rather than functioning primarily as an annual budgeting exercise.

### 

### **Financial Leadership \& Stewardship**


 Provide executive oversight, collaboratively with the accounting and business functions, of the school's financial operations. Lead the development of annual and long\-range operating and capital budgets in partnership

**Department**
--------------

College of Business\-Office
**About the University**

  

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.  



Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic\-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first\-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.  



  

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world\-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.  



  

**FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute Vision and Mission**

  

The vision of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute is that MSU Denver students, alumni, faculty, staff, and community partners will have access to the knowledge, resources, experiences, and support they need to understand, enter, and lead within the affordable housing field.  



  

The mission of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute is to advance affordable housing education, workforce development, community engagement, and industry\-connected learning. The Institute prepares students and community members to contribute meaningfully to affordable housing, real estate, finance, policy, development, and community impact through academic programs, non\-credit programming, experiential learning, partnerships, and applied industry engagement.  



  

**Position Summary**

  

The College of Business at MSU Denver seeks a forward\-thinking, visionary, and experienced leader to serve as the next Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute. The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute (AHI) provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and academic integration for MSU Denver’s interdisciplinary affordable housing initiative. This is a 12\-month appointment with ongoing, year\-round administrative and instructional duties reporting to the Dean of the College of Business.  



  

The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute serves as the academic, strategic, and community\-facing leader for affordable housing education, workforce development, industry engagement, non\-credit programming, and interdisciplinary academic integration. Housed within the College of Business but operating with an interdisciplinary and collaborative focus, the Institute supports students, faculty, community partners, housing professionals, developers, financial institutions, nonprofit organizations, public agencies, and industry stakeholders by connecting affordable housing knowledge with education, career pathways, applied learning, and community impact.  



  

The Executive Director is responsible for advancing the Institute’s role as a regional leader in affordable housing education and workforce development. The Executive Director will help position MSU Denver as a distinctive public urban university partner for affordable housing finance, policy, development, management, and community\-centered housing solutions. The Executive Director will also support student success, professional mobility, and industry engagement by helping students and working professionals develop the knowledge, skills, experiences, and relationships needed to contribute to the affordable housing sector. The Executive Director will work closely with faculty, college leadership, college and school partners, University Advancement, C2 Hub, the Affordable Housing Industry Navigator, the AHI Advisory Council, and external stakeholders.  



  

**Responsibilities**

  

Center Executive Director \- Leadership and Strategic Management of the Center (70%)  



  

Strategic Leadership \& Operations


* Provide overall leadership and vision for AHI aligned with the College of Business strategic priorities
* Establish annual goals, program strategy, and operational processes
* Oversee day\-to\-day operations, budgeting, and program execution
Collaborate with the C2 Hub and the AH Industry Navigator to recruit and enroll students into programming  
* 

  

Fundraising \& Advancement


* Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with donors, foundations, and public agencies
* Partner with University Advancement to secure grants, sponsorships, and philanthropic support
Prepare proposals, manage funded projects, and ensure reporting compliance  
* 

  

Community \& Industry Partnerships


* Build and maintain relationships with developers, financial institutions, nonprofits, and government agencies
* Serve as MSU Denver’s representative in housing coalitions and industry forums
Convene events such as summits, panels, and practitioner workshops  
* 

  

Non\-Credit Program Development


* Lead development and promotion of non\-credit programs (certificates, workshops, executive education)
* Recruit instructors and ensure program quality

**The LCMS Mission**

"In grateful response to God's grace and empowered by the Holy Spirit through Word and Sacraments, the mission of The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod is vigorously to make known the love of Christ by word and deed within our churches, communities, and world."


**Department Profile**

The LCMS Board of Directors (BOD) is vested with the general management and supervision of the Synod’s business and legal affairs, including the review and coordination of the policies and directives of the Synod authorized by its Constitution, Bylaws and resolutions and of the plans and policies of the Synod’s boards and commissions. It provides for the administration, financial and operational support, and accountability of the activities of corporate Synod and the oversight and coordination of the same for the broader Synod, as all together pursue the objectives of the Synod as stated in Const. Art. III: to conserve and promote the unity of the true faith, strengthening the witness of Synod members, providing for church worker training and care, for works of mercy, for Christian education, for resourcing of confessional unity, uniformity and variety in responsible practices and customs, ecclesiastical supervision, and protection of congregations and workers in the exercise of their duties and maintenance of their rights.


The Chief Operating Officer of the Synod is an officer of the Synod (Const. Art. XI A) and the board’s executive, serving at the board’s direction in successive three\-year terms as appointed, performing directly or supervising the following functions (Bylaws 3\.4\.1, 3\.4\.1\.3\):


* Administration of the financial affairs of the Synod, excluding the synodwide corporate entities, the districts, the Concordia Plans, and Concordia Plan Services. This includes supervision of all financial\-related areas, including accounts receivable, cash receipts, general and cost accounting, internal audit, budgeting, and corporate insurance. This includes responsibility for corporate Synod finance (including service as Treasurer) and executive performance of the board’s oversight and limited supervision of finance for agencies of the Synod outside corporate Synod, such as the seminaries and universities, synodwide corporate entities, districts, etc.
* Administration of the responsibilities given to the Board of Directors in the Constitution, Bylaws, and resolutions of the Synod, now including non\-theological, non\-messaging aspects of communications and fundraising.

The Chief Operating Officer also works together closely with the Chief Mission Officer, who serves at the direction of the President of the Synod, in carrying out the programmatic, administrative, and financial functions of the national Synod (Bylaw 3\.4\.1\.4\) and serves as part of the Synod Administrative Team (Bylaws 3\.5\.1–3\.5\.1\.1\).


The Chief Operating Officer shall be selected with the consultation and concurrence of the President of Synod.


**Reporting Relationships**

* Reports to the convention as a Synod officer
* Reports to the BOD, typically through the Board Chair
* Serves as part of the Administrative Team (Bylaw 3\.5\.1\), which is under the leadership and oversight of the President.

**Position Summary**

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as the senior executive responsible for the oversight, coordination, and integration of the organization’s operational, administrative, financial, and compliance functions. Acting on behalf of the Board of Directors and in coordination with the President, the COO ensures that all organizational activities are executed efficiently, effectively, accountably, and in alignment with the Synod’s mission, governing policies, and strategic priorities.


The COO provides leadership across areas of corporate services, financial management, human resources, legal compliance, and organizational infrastructure.


**Essential Job Functions**

* **Executive Leadership \& Governance**
	+ Serve as chief operating executive responsible for implementing Board decisions and organizational strategy for business, financial, legal, and administrative operations of the corporate Synod.
	+ Advise and support the Board of Directors and President on operational and financial matters.
	+ Prepare Board agendas, reports, and materials in coordination with leadership.
	+ Ensure compliance with governing documents (Constitution, Bylaws, policies, and civil law).
	+ Maintain communication between Board and executive leadership.
	+ Serves, unless the board designates otherwise, on the following corporate entity boards: Concordia Plan Services, Lutheran Church Extension Fund, LCMS Foundation, Concordia Publishing House, Concordia University System, and on the investment committee of the Concordia Plans and Concordia Plan Services.
	+ Serves on the following international Board(s)/Committee(s): China Evangelical Lutheran Church – Legal Corporation (CELC\-LC).
	+ Serves on the Commission on Handbook.
	+ Direct supervision of \~4 executives and an administrator, indirect of 7–9 director/managers and 40–114 staff in an organization with headcount of 191 domestic, 103 international (and responsibilities with regard to universities, seminaries, entities, and agencies outside corporate Synod).
* **Operational Oversight**
	+ Direct and coordinate, principally through executives and directors, day\-to\-day operations of the organization.
	+ Lead enterprise\-wide operational planning aligned with strategic goals.
	+ Ensure collaboration across departments, entities, and mission units related to the business, financial, legal, and administrative operations of corporate Synod.
	+ Improve organizational efficiency, systems, and service delivery.
	+ Oversee facilities, event planning, procurement, and administrative services.
	+ Serve as convention manager and be responsible to the President of Synod as outlined in Bylaw 3\.1\.9\.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**About the Cotton Charitable Foundation**

The Cotton Charitable Foundation provides families facing a terminal or serious illness with a special place to spend time together, create meaningful memories, and experience moments of joy and connection during an extraordinarily difficult time through Taylor’s Place, a private sanctuary just west of Houston.

Through the generosity of donors, corporate partners, foundations, and event supporters, Taylor’s Place provides families with an opportunity to step away from the challenges of illness and simply be together.

The Cotton Charitable Foundation is entering an exciting period of growth. The organization is seeking a dynamic, relationship\-driven Director of Development to build upon its strong philanthropic foundation, expand its donor base, increase revenue, and create a sustainable development program for the future.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development will lead all aspects of fundraising, development, marketing, and communications for the Cotton Charitable Foundation. This is a hands\-on leadership position for an experienced fundraiser who can develop strategy while actively cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors.

The Director will be responsible for generating revenue through a diversified portfolio of individual giving, major gifts, corporate partnerships, foundation support, special events, and other philanthropic opportunities. In addition to growing philanthropic revenue, the Director will strengthen Taylor’s Place’s visibility and brand through strategic communications, digital engagement, social media, website management, print materials, and compelling storytelling. The Director will ensure that the organization’s external presence effectively communicates its mission, impact, and opportunities for philanthropic support.

A key priority will be growing the organization beyond its existing fundraising model. The Foundation currently hosts one primary fundraising event, and the Director will evaluate and develop additional events and engagement opportunities that generate revenue while introducing new families, donors, corporations, and community partners to the mission.

The ideal candidate will be equally comfortable sitting across the table from a major donor, developing a corporate sponsorship proposal, writing a foundation grant, working with volunteers, and creating a compelling fundraising event.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Development Strategy \& Revenue Growth**

* Develop and implement a comprehensive annual and multi\-year development strategy designed to sustain and grow Taylor’s Place.
* Establish annual fundraising goals, revenue projections, strategies, and measurable performance indicators.
* Develop a diversified fundraising portfolio that reduces reliance on any single source of revenue.
* Identify new sources of philanthropic support and opportunities to expand the organization’s donor base.
* Create and maintain a strong pipeline of prospective donors, corporate partners, foundations, and sponsors.
* Regularly evaluate fundraising results and adjust strategies to maximize opportunities.
* Work closely with the Executive Director to align fundraising priorities with the organization’s strategic vision.

**Major Gifts \& Individual Philanthropy**

* Develop and manage a portfolio of major\-gift prospects and donors.
* Create individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for prospective and current major donors.
* Build relationships with individuals who have the capacity and inclination to make significant investments in Taylor’s Place.
* Partner with Foundation leadership, board members, and key volunteers on donor introductions and solicitations.
* Develop opportunities for donors to make transformational gifts to support Taylor’s Place and its future growth.
* Strengthen annual giving and identify opportunities to move annual donors into higher levels of engagement and philanthropy.

**Corporate \& Foundation Relations**

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate partners and sponsors.
* Develop meaningful partnerships with businesses that align with Taylor’s Place’s mission and values.
* Create compelling sponsorship opportunities that provide meaningful engagement and visibility for corporate partners.
* Research and pursue foundation funding opportunities aligned with Taylor’s Place programs and priorities.
* Oversee grant proposals, letters of inquiry, reports, renewals, and funder communications.
* Develop long\-term relationships with corporate and foundation partners rather than focusing solely on individual funding requests.

**Events \& Special Events Growth**

Taylor’s Place currently has one established fundraising event. A major responsibility of this position will be to thoughtfully expand the organization’s event strategy.

* Provide strategic leadership for the existing fundraising event, maximizing revenue, sponsorships, attendance, and donor engagement.
* Evaluate the feasibility and potential return on investment of additional fundraising events.
* Develop and implement new events and fundraising experiences that introduce Taylor’s Place to new audiences.
* Develop event sponsorship opportunities and secure corporate and individual support.
* Recruit and engage event committees, volunteers, community leaders, and ambassadors.
* Ensure events serve not only as fundraising opportunities but also as vehicles for donor cultivation, community awareness, and long\-term relationship building.
* Establish financial and performance metrics for each event and evaluate results annually.

**Donor Stewardship \& Engagement**

* Create a comprehensive donor stewardship program that ensures supporters understand the impact of their generosity.
* Develop personalized communications and engagement strategies for key donors.
* Ensure timely acknowledgments, impact reports, invitations, updates, and other donor communications.
* Work with staff and F

jobs.title: Program Director, Executive Education (6 month term)
jobs.description:
Company Description  

  

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world\-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.


**Why join the Harvard Kennedy School?**


The John F. Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University is one of 12 graduate and professional schools at the university. Harvard Kennedy School’s mission is to improve public policy and leadership so people can live in societies that are more safe, free, just, and sustainably prosperous. By combining cutting\-edge research, the teaching of outstanding students, and direct interaction with practitioners, we have an impact on solving public problems that no other institution can match. When you work at Harvard Kennedy School, you make a difference.

  

  

Job Description  

  

Harvard Kennedy School Executive Education (HKS Exec Ed) is the premier worldwide source for executive\-level leadership development focused on public service. Exec Ed operates as a department within HKS and provides 80\+ programs ranging from 1 to 4 weeks in length to 4500\+ participants each year. Programs are delivered online, in\-person, or a combination of both, and are offered as open enrollment via an admissions process or as custom programs focused on the needs of public service or government organizations, sponsors, or donors. Exec Ed is a critical piece of the HKS mission to improve public policy and leadership so people can live in societies that are more safe, free, just, and sustainably prosperous. Programs are led by faculty and attract accomplished public leaders from around the world, with roles in the government, nonprofit, multilateral, and corporate sectors.


Harvard Kennedy School (HKS) seeks a Program Director to join our Executive Education team. Reporting to the Senior Director, Program Management, the Program Director manages an assigned portfolio of 6\-8 executive education programs with budget responsibilities of approx. $3M. Programs include both new and existing. The Program Director is responsible for leading all aspects of assigned programs, including coordinating faculty effort, ensuring participant satisfaction, managing operational staff, grant/gift submission and reporting as needed and achieving financial targets, to ensure that Executive Education programs are delivered with excellence. We seek collaborative, adaptable candidates who love the details of programs and events, are driven by working with others on a fast\-paced team and are excited about having an impact on our world by supporting leaders from around the country and the world. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive team culture and seek candidates who share our values and commitment.

  

  

**Job\-Specific Responsibilities:**

As a Program Director, you will represent HKS, Executive Education to faculty and program participants in your portfolio of programs as well as external partners/vendors. In this capacity, you will manage:


PROGRAM MANAGEMENT


* Manage all aspects of admissions and enrollment process, including admission decisions and fellowship/tuition assistance award decisions.
* Review, enhance and implement existing marketing and outreach strategies, in coordination with the Executive Education marketing team and Senior Director. Strategy may include direct mail, conference participation, third party funding relationships, recruiting meetings, and/or sales visits to target groups.
* Key contributor during the launch process of new programming.
* Manages communication strategy and processes with prospective participants.
* Organize reports and data for faculty chair(s) and Senior Director of program management.

PROGRAM DELIVERY


* Lead a delivery team in 6\-8 new and existing programs, ensuring all aspects of program development and implementation are planned, managed, and executed at the highest standards.
* Direct each program’s operations, including all aspects of logistics, faculty relationships, curriculum management, and coordination with custom clients, as needed.
* Develop strong working relationships with faculty chair; staff faculty chair for program activity as appropriate; Consulting with faculty chair on major program related activity and/or decisions as needed. Responsible for informing faculty chair about standards within EE, such as faculty comp guidelines and the process related to the hiring of teaching assistants.
* Negotiate with new and existing external vendors, sign contracts on behalf of the program for offsite events.
* Take the lead in anticipating and resolving issues and escalating to the senior director as needed.
* Manage processes to ensure program participants are supported before, during and after the programs, online and in person.
* Act as project manager for new and existing programming.
* Review program evaluations with faculty chair(s) to determine and implement changes in program content for future offerings.

OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP


* Exercise financial management and oversight of assigned programs, including budgeting, faculty compensation and fulfilling all required reporting processes, including financial reconciliation and the Program Review \& Outlook (PRO) process. Track and comply with any external reporting requirements; for example, with third party payers.
* Responsible for grant/gift submissions and reporting.
* Seek opportunities to develop and lead improvements to standard operating procedures across all programs.
* Maintain and clearly communicate to program leadership key data on enrollment, content, program highlights, performance, etc.

TEAM MANAGEMENT


* Manage staff assigned to program; ensuring a high level of professionalism, teamwork and focus on customer service. Review staff work; completes program staff evaluations after each program.

**Full\-Time, Exempt**

The Executive Director leads Recovery Rowan County's day\-to\-day operations, staff, and long\-term direction. This person directs day\-to\-day service delivery for grants, coordinates peer staff, and works closely with the Project Director on grant compliance and reporting. Both roles report to the RRC Board of Directors.

**Reports To**

* RRC Board of Directors

**Coordinates Closely With**

* Project Director
* Board Treasurer and contracted CPA
* RCDC, ARIA, and other project partners

**Supervises**

* RRC peer staff and volunteers
* Peer recovery positions
* Recovery Corps members

**Location**

* RRC office, Morehead, KY
* Regular travel to partner sites in Rowan, Bath, and Morgan Counties
* Occasional out\-of\-area travel

**Compensation**

* To be set by the Board, informed by the organization's overall budget
* Starting at $52,500 per year

**Qualifications**

**Required Experience**

* "Lived Experience" – a minimum of five years in recovery with an identifiable recovery pathway
* A minimum of three years' experience providing peer support, recovery coaching, or related services
* At least three years of nonprofit, human services, or program management experience
* Experience with, or demonstrated ability to quickly learn, performance data and outcome\-tracking systems
* Valid Kentucky driver's license
* Knowledge of recovery ecosystems and experience accessing their various components
* Desire and ability to develop an organizational culture of recovery

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience working in the field of reentry
* Experience supervising staff, ideally including peer support specialists or other recovery workforce
* Experience managing an organizational or program budget of $250,000 or more, including experience administering restricted or grant\-funded dollars
* Experience with fundraising and grant writing strongly preferred

Education

* High school diploma or GED required
* Bachelor's degree preferred

Skills

* Very strong written and verbal communication skills
* Ability to learn project management and development
* Ability to negotiate, secure, and execute collaborative agreements, including MOUs and subaward or contract relationships
* Comfortable managing competing priorities across organizational leadership and grant\-specific compliance work
* Ability to provide strong leadership and supervisory skills in a peer led organization

Please send a Resume \& Cover Letter to:

Pay: From $52,500\.00 per year

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

jobs.title: Executive Director - AgeBetter
jobs.description:
**Executive Director \- AgeBetter**
***Please note:****Recruitment for this position will be led by Attic Angel in partnership with Oakwood Village.*
AgeBetter, Inc. is a nonprofit organization located in Dane County, Wisconsin. Founded In 2005, AgeBetter has two sponsoring nonprofit organizations, Oakwood Village and Attic Angel. AgeBetter is the parent, organization and founder of Safe at Home and SAIL – Sharing Active Independent Lives. The mission of AgeBetter and its programs is to enhance the health, wellness, and independence of older adults in collaboration with older adults, their families, caregivers, healthcare providers, community\-based aging services, payers, and educators.
We are seeking the next leader of AgeBetter, an organization that has served the Madison community for more than 20 years. AgeBetter is best known for its SAIL (Supporting Active Independent Lives) program and, more recently, Safe at Home. The ideal candidate will be passionate about bringing people together, meeting individuals where they are, and fostering a strong sense of community and belonging. This leader will bring a strong background in leadership and relationship\-building, along with experience identifying and securing donations and grants to strengthen and expand the programs and services AgeBetter provides.

  

***Position Location:****Oakwood Village University Woods Campus*
*6205 Mineral Point Rd*
*Madison, WI 53705*
**Mission Statement:**
AgeBetter Inc.'s mission is to collaborate with older individuals, their families, caregivers, physicians, payers, service providers, and educators to enhance their health, wellness, independence, and overall quality of life.
**Position Overview:**The Executive Director (ED) serves as the face of AgeBetter and is responsible for managing the programs offered within this organization including the SAIL and Safe at Home programs. This work includes membership recruitment, outreach, fundraising, new service development, operations and administration, and working with the Board on strategic planning and finance. The position requires working with a wide range of local and, in some cases, national organizations and institutions, and with the residents of Dane County. The ED will be responsible for establishing and managing a small team environment including hiring and managing support staff.
This position reports to the Board of Directors.
**Essential Responsibilities (not meant to be an all\-inclusive list):*** Assure the delivery of outstanding member services.
* Maintain and expand membership through recruitment of new members and membership renewals.
* Collaborate with the Board of Directors to develop and maintain strategic and tactical plans to guide the organization.
* Recruit and manage volunteers participating in SAIL programs; determine and supervise volunteer activities.
* Lead AgeBetter programs (SAIL \& Safe at Home) fundraising activities, developing and implementing fundraising and marketing plans, identifying new funding sources, writing grant proposals and creating strategies for donor solicitation.
* Develop partnerships with organizations that can provide services to members.
* Ensure effective systems to manage and regularly evaluate program components, so as to measure successes that can be effectively communicated to the board, the funders and other constituents.
* Serve as the principal public relations representative when interacting with media, funding sources, government agencies and community groups.
* Deepen and refine all aspects of communications\-from web presence to external relations with the goal of creating a stronger brand.
* Work independently to establish an efficient, organized business compliant with regulations; maintain accurate, confidential records; recruit and effectively manage a small staff; maintain an accurate database of members, member assistance, referral information and service providers, donors and grant providers.
* Recommend policies and procedures to produce maximum utilization of resources and optimal service levels at minimum cost.
* Understand and effectively carry out policies as set by the AgeBetter Board of Directors.
* Track organization income and expenditures, in consultation with the Board of Directors.
* Attend all Board meetings, implement Board directives.

**Essential Qualifications:**
* Skill in overseeing organizational finances, including budget formulation and execution.
* Experience with laws and regulations that affect services to older people.
* An understanding of the needs of people age 50 and older as they age in their homes.
* Ability to communicate persuasively in speech and writing.
* Ability to develop collaborative relationships with a variety of professionals from City and County officials and service providers, Village Network, etc.

**Education/Training/Experience:**
* Minimum BA/BS degree with five (5\) to seven (7\) years of senior management experience in a non\-profit setting preferable with experience in fundraising, communication, business and/or social work. A Master’s degree in a relevant field is desirable.
* Significant work with older adults, social service or home and community based service environments is strongly recommended.
* Broad knowledge of nonprofit fundraising and marketing techniques, donor and membership development.
* Experience with budgeting, basic accounting and other financials concerning
* nonprofits.
* Proficient in Microsoft 365 including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Teams. Club Express experience or other membership software experience preferred.

jobs.title: Director of Development & External Affairs
jobs.description:
**JOB TITLE:** Director of Development \& External Affairs

**DEPARTMENT:** M\&G

**EDUCATION LEVEL:** 4 Year Degree

**REPORTS TO:** CEO

**TRAVEL:** Occasional local travel may be required

**FLSA STATUS:** Exempt

**SUPERVISORY ROLE:** Yes

**ABOUT ACCESSHEALTH**

AccessHealth is a private, not\-for\-profit Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) serving Fort Bend and Waller Counties, TX since 1975 providing integrated, affordable healthcare to \~20,000 patients annually across 17 locations. A 2025 HRSA National Quality Leader and NCQA Patient\-Centered Medical Home.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Development \& External Affairs leads AccessHealth’s fundraising, external partnerships, community engagement, and strategic communications efforts. The position is responsible for expanding philanthropic support, strengthening community and referral partnerships, and increasing AccessHealth’s visibility throughout the communities it serves.

Working closely with the CEO and organizational leadership, the Director develops and executes strategies that strengthen AccessHealth’s financial sustainability, community presence, and relationships with donors, corporations, foundations, healthcare organizations, government stakeholders, and community partners.

**ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Fundraising, Donor Development \& Events**

* Develop and execute AccessHealth’s annual fundraising and development strategy.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, corporate partners, foundations, and other philanthropic supporters.
* Manage donor development activities from prospect identification through solicitation and stewardship.
* Identify and pursue grant opportunities and oversee grant development, submission, reporting, and compliance.
* Plan and oversee fundraising campaigns, sponsorship opportunities, donor engagement activities, and signature fundraising events.
* Develop strategies to increase donor retention, recurring giving, corporate sponsorships, and philanthropic revenue.
* Maintain accurate donor and fundraising records within the organization’s CRM or donor management system.
* Establish fundraising goals and provide regular development reports to the CEO and Board of Directors.
* Support the Board Development Committee and related development initiatives.

**Strategic Partnerships \& External Affairs**

* Develop and maintain strategic relationships with hospitals, healthcare organizations, employers, schools, faith\-based organizations, nonprofits, and other community partners.
* Identify partnership opportunities that increase awareness of AccessHealth services and strengthen appropriate patient referral pathways.
* Build and maintain relationships with government officials, community leaders, and other key stakeholders in coordination with the CEO.
* Represent AccessHealth at chambers of commerce, community coalitions, healthcare forums, and other external meetings and events.
* Monitor community needs and external trends and identify opportunities that support AccessHealth’s mission and strategic priorities.

**Communications, Brand \& Digital Strategy**

* Oversee external communications and marketing initiatives that strengthen awareness of AccessHealth’s services, programs, impact, and mission.
* Direct digital marketing and search visibility strategies, including SEO, social media, website visibility, and emerging AI\-driven search technologies.
* Coordinate media relations, public announcements, and external communications in collaboration with the CEO and organizational leadership.
* Oversee the development of impact reports, donor communications, community materials, and other external\-facing publications.
* Monitor marketing and engagement performance and recommend strategies to strengthen AccessHealth’s external reach and visibility.

**Leadership \& Administration**

* Serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO on fundraising, external partnerships, community engagement, and development opportunities.
* Establish and monitor goals and key performance indicators for development and external affairs activities.
* Develop and manage applicable departmental budgets and resources.
* Collaborate across departments to ensure development and external affairs initiatives align with organizational priorities.
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned by the Chief Executive Officer.

**EDUCATION/LICENSURE/CERTIFICATION QUALIFICATIONS:**

**REQUIRED:**

* 7\+ years in nonprofit development, healthcare business development, or comparable external\-facing leadership
* Proven track record: personally closed gifts, grants, or sponsorships of $25,000\+; managed an annual fund of $500,000\+
