jobs.title: Executive Director, Together for Chester, Inc.
jobs.description:
**Executive Director, Together for Chester Free Clinic**

**Reporting to: Board of Directors**

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director, Together for Chester Free Clinic provides strategic and operational leadership for a portfolio of community‑based health initiatives, including oversight of a pro bono health clinic serving uninsured and under‑served populations. This role is responsible for program design, implementation, evaluation, staff and volunteer recruitment and supervision, and sustainability across community health programs that advance access, equity, and health outcomes. The Director collaborates closely with clinical leaders, community partners, volunteers, and organizational leadership to ensure high‑quality, culturally responsive, and patient‑centered services.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership \& Program Oversight**

* Provide vision, leadership, and oversight for community health programs, including a pro bono/free health clinic.
* Develop and implement program strategies aligned with organizational mission, community needs assessments, and health equity goals.
* Establish program goals, outcomes, and performance metrics; regularly evaluate effectiveness and impact.
* Identify opportunities for program growth, innovation, and integration across services.

**Pro Bono Health Clinic Leadership**

* Oversee day‑to‑day operations of the pro bono health clinic, ensuring safe, efficient, and high‑quality care delivery.
* Manage clinic workflows, scheduling, and coordination of services.
* Recruit, onboard, train, and support volunteer clinicians, students, and non‑clinical volunteers.
* Ensure clinic operations comply with applicable regulations, licensure requirements, and patient privacy standards.
* Serve as liaison to clinical partners, academic institutions, and professional organizations supporting pro bono care.

**Community Engagement \& Partnerships**

* Build and maintain strong relationships with community‑based organizations, health systems, public health agencies, and social service partners.
* Represent the organization in community coalitions, advisory groups, and public forums.
* Strengthen referral pathways and connections to wrap‑around services addressing social drivers of health.

**Equity, Quality \& Patient Experience**

* Advance health equity by reducing barriers to care and centering community voice and lived experience.
* Ensure programs are culturally responsive, trauma‑informed, and inclusive.
* Lead continuous quality improvement initiatives informed by data, patient feedback, and best practices.

**Financial, Administrative \& Grant Management**

* Develop and manage program budgets; monitor expenses and resource utilization.
* Support grant development, implementation, reporting, and compliance for community health programs.
* Contribute to fundraising efforts by providing program data, outcomes, and impact narratives.

**Team \& Operational Management**

* Supervise program staff and support a collaborative, mission‑driven team culture.
* Develop and maintain program policies, procedures, and documentation.
* Use data systems and reporting tools to track performance and inform decision‑making.

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in public health, health administration, social work, nursing, or a related field
* 7\+ years of experience in community health, nonprofit program management, or healthcare operations.
* Demonstrated experience working with under‑served populations and community‑based health programs.
* Experience managing or partnering with volunteer or pro bono clinical services.
* Strong leadership, project management, and organizational skills.
* Knowledge of healthcare compliance, patient privacy, and quality standards.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience overseeing a free or pro bono health clinic.
* Familiarity with electronic health records, data reporting, and program evaluation.
* Grant writing or grants management experience.
* Bilingual or multilingual skills relevant to the populations served.

**Working Conditions**

* May include occasional evening or weekend hours for clinics or community events.
* Combination of on‑site and administrative work, depending on program needs.
* Local travel for community engagement and partner meetings.

**Job status:** Fulltime

Pay: $33\.00 \- $36\.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Professional development assistance

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Chester, PA 19013

jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Ignite your passion for product innovation by leading customer\-centric development, inspiring solutions, and shaping the future with your strategic vision and influence.
As a Content Platform Executive Director at JPMorganChase within our Digital Channels team, you will bring a platform mindset and own the strategy and roadmap for an enterprise content platform that transforms how teams and agents deliver high\-quality content faster, with strong governance, reliability, personalization and measurable outcomes. You will partner across technology, experience, data, and architecture to scale platform capabilities and establish repeatable patterns that improve delivery speed and consistency. You will lead a high\-performing team and influence senior stakeholders by translating business needs into platform priorities that drive adoption and value.
**Job responsibilities**
* Own the enterprise content platform vision, roadmap and prioritization to deliver measurable improvements in publishing speed, reuse, and platform reliability
* Lead end\-to\-end platform product execution from discovery through delivery, balancing modernization, operational excellence, and new capability rollout
* Build, mentor, and scale a product team of approximately 15–20, establishing clear roles, decision rights, and an effective operating cadence
* Drive the evolution of agentic capabilities, including authoring workflows, templates, component model, content governance, publishing processes, and self\-service enablement
* Establish platform standards and reusable delivery patterns (for example, reference implementations, guardrails, integration patterns, and documentation) to accelerate adoption across teams
* Define and manage KPIs that demonstrate platform value (for example, adoption, time\-to\-publish, reuse, reliability, and internal user satisfaction) and use them to guide investment decisions
* Embed risk, privacy, and security requirements into platform workflows in a way that reduces friction and improves auditability and compliance readiness
* Partner with engineering and operations to strengthen platform resiliency, manage incidents and problem management themes, and improve service health over time
* Influence senior stakeholders across the firm by communicating tradeoffs transparently and aligning priorities to business outcomes
**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**
* Formal training or certification on product management concepts and 10\+ years applied experience
* Demonstrated experience owning platform strategy, roadmaps, and outcomes for enterprise\-scale products used by a diverse set of teams
* Strong expertise across the product development lifecycle, including discovery, value definition, delivery, and ongoing optimization
* Proven ability to lead and coach managers and senior product leaders while building a high\-performance culture
* Deep experience with enterprise content management capabilities (workflow, metadata and taxonomy, governance, publishing, and integrations)
* Executive\-level communication skills with a track record of influencing decisions across technology and business stakeholders
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills, including defining success metrics and using data to drive prioritization and outcomes
**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills**
* Experience leading platform products operating in a federated delivery model across many internal teams
* Experience delivering large modernization or migration programs, including consolidation and deprecation strategies
* Background delivering products in regulated or highly controlled environments with strong governance and auditability expectations
* Recognized expertise in enterprise content platforms and operating models, including adoption strategy and change management
* Experience improving platform self\-service through documentation, enablement, and scalable intake processes
  
  

**ABOUT US**  

  

  

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.


We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission\-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on\-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.


We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. **Make a difference in our community and join the Sarasota Housing Authority (SHA) Team!**

Since 1938, Sarasota Housing Authority (SHA) has been committed to providing quality affordable housing to enhance the lives of our residents and promote their independence. Our professional team members provide housing assistance to over 2,000 low\-income families in Sarasota. In addition to affordable housing, SHA endeavors to help our families access appropriate services to improve their lives and is an award\-winning industry leader in early childhood education. SHA is also a HUD High Performer in every category, for several years running. For more information on SHA, visit www.sarasotahousing.org.

SHA is committed to providing our team members with a flexible work\-life balance that increases their quality of life and well\-being.

**Become part of the SHA team and enjoy:**

* A four\-day (40\-hour) condensed work week, Monday–Thursday schedule
* Generous paid time off program
* Twelve paid holidays annually
* 100% company\-paid medical, dental, and vision for employee only, starting on day one!
* Employer Match Deferred Compensation Plan of 100% of deferrals up to 5\.4% of pay; if deferrals are 5\.5% of pay or more, the match will be 7\.5% of pay

**What We Are Looking For:**

SHA is seeking an experienced and relationship\-driven Development Director to lead fundraising and external relations for our affiliated 501(c)(3\). This newly created leadership position offers the opportunity to build and grow a comprehensive development program that advances the Authority's mission and expands support for transformative initiatives such as Youth Thrive.

The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker and exceptional communicator with a proven ability to secure grants, cultivate major donors, and build lasting partnerships throughout the community. This individual is self\-motivated, highly organized, and passionate about connecting philanthropic investment with meaningful community impact.

**In this Role, You Will:**

* Develop and implement a comprehensive annual fundraising and resource development strategy
* Research, prepare, and submit competitive grant applications to foundations, corporations, and government funding sources

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors and philanthropic partners

* Represent SHA and Youth Thrive at community meetings, networking events, and public engagements
* Build strategic partnerships with community organizations, businesses, foundations, and civic leaders

* Support development\-related marketing efforts, including social media and community outreach
* Perform other related duties as assigned

**What You Need:**

* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, communications, public administration, or a related field required
* CFRE (Certified Fund Raising Executive) credential or active pursuit preferred
* Demonstrated track record of securing grant funding and/or philanthropic contributions, with examples of successful fundraising outcomes.
* Five(5\) or more years of progressively responsible fundraising, grant writing, or nonprofit development experience
* Demonstrated success securing grant funding and cultivating donor relationships
* Experience managing multiple projects and competing deadlines
* Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills
* Experience with donor management or CRM software preferred
* Exceptional relationship\-building, networking, and organizational skills
* Valid Florida driver's license with the ability to be insured under SHA's fleet insurance policy

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer (F/T, remote)
jobs.description:
**About The Chronicle of Philanthropy**



The Chronicle of Philanthropy is the leading source of journalism, opinion, actionable insights, and training for nonprofit and foundation leaders, fundraising executives, and other professionals who drive social impact.


As our growing organization seeks to expand its work after raising $9 million to transition to nonprofit status, the Chronicle is now seeking a fundraising professional who can attract private support to enable the Chronicle to do more to help nonprofits thrive and ensure the public has a strong understanding of the importance of philanthropy to communities everywhere. Beyond your work to raise at least $2 million a year, you’ll have the opportunity to build a fundraising team and plan for a campaign to make our 40th anniversary in 2028\.


This is a rare chance to become a key player in expanding one of the leading organizations in the social sector.


**The Opportunity**


The chief development officer is a senior, strategic position who will drive The Chronicle’s work to attract foundation grants and explore other sources of philanthropic support, especially major gifts. The successful fundraising leader will understand our special role in providing independent journalism and professional development to nonprofits and foundations and in complementing our strong earned\-revenue efforts, which represent about 80 percent of our budget.


The chief development officer will work closely with our CEO, chief revenue officer, and chief content officer to:


* Set our philanthropic strategy
* Develop our case for general operating support and innovation funding
* Cultivate foundations and other supporters
* Build a culture that ensures long\-term fundraising success

The right candidate is a seasoned development executive who is both a strategist and a doer: comfortable writing a six\-figure letter of intent one day and building a multi\-year revenue forecast on the next.


Beyond building a strong fundraising plan for the next three years, you’ll also assemble a team who can assist you and the rest of the organization. To aid you in that work, you’ll have an opportunity to gain insights from a feasibility study the Bridgespan Group is undertaking on our behalf.
 

**Key Responsibilities**


* Strategy \& Leadership
* Design and implement a comprehensive development strategy, building on our successful foundation grant seeking
* Expand the number of foundations who provide support to the Chronicle, focusing both on support for specific programs and unrestricted funding
* Serve as a thought partner to the CEO in articulating programs, new initiatives, and the overarching impact and ambitions of The Chronicle.
* Examine the potential for attracting support from individuals, focusing on major and planned gifts

**Lead the Next Era of Tropical Agricultural Research**

**The Hawaiʻi Agriculture Research Center (HARC)** seeks an entrepreneurial, collaborative, scientific executive to lead the organization through a pivotal period of transition and into its next era of growth and impact. Building on more than a century of applied agricultural research in Hawaiʻi, HARC has repeatedly evolved with Hawaiʻi agriculture, from its origins serving the sugar industry to a diversified nonprofit research organization. Today, HARC has an opportunity to again define how its scientific capabilities, facilities, partnerships, and distinctive tropical setting can address the changing needs of agriculture in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

**About HARC**

HARC is a private 501(c)(3\) nonprofit agricultural research organization headquartered at the Kunia Research Station in Waipahu, Oʻahu. Its team of scientists, agronomists, foresters, conservationists, and technical experts works across five core research divisions. Current work includes crop improvement and breeding, coffee leaf rust resistance, agrivoltaics, native forest restoration, crop propagation and tissue culture, and applied research supporting Hawaiʻi producers and natural\-resource managers.

**The Opportunity**

HARC is at an institutional inflection point. The organization seeks a leader who respects and learns from its history and deep institutional knowledge while recognizing that agricultural science, crop biotechnology, research funding, technology, and Hawaiʻi’s agricultural economy continue to change. The next Executive Director will help HARC consolidate a compelling mission and long\-term vision, establish a focused and financially sustainable research strategy, and build organizational alignment around that direction.

**This is a CEO\-level opportunity for a leader who can unite** scientific credibility, organizational leadership, financial and operational discipline, and external partnership development with the vision and energy to help shape HARC’s future. Following more than three decades of continuity in executive leadership, the next Executive Director will work collaboratively with HARC’s senior project leaders, staff, Board, producers, community partners, funders, industry, universities, and government agencies to clarify strategic direction, focus research priorities, strengthen financial sustainability, and position HARC for its next chapter.

**Key Responsibilities**

● **Organizational leadership, mission \& strategy:** Lead a collaborative process with the Board, senior project leaders, staff, and key partners to refine HARC’s mission, establish a compelling long\-term vision, set research and organizational priorities, and translate them into measurable plans and outcomes.

● **Financial sustainability \& business development:** Build a durable financial model by aligning resources with strategic priorities, strengthening existing programs, diversifying federal, state, philanthropic, industry, and fee\-for\-service revenue, and developing new sponsored\-research and partnership opportunities.

● **Research portfolio \& scientific innovation:** Work with HARC’s scientific leaders to evaluate and focus the research portfolio, support high\-quality applied research, identify opportunities in new crops and emerging technologies, and help develop competitive grants, contracts, collaborations, and programs with meaningful producer and community impact.

● **People, culture \& organizational alignment:** Build a high\-performing, collaborative organization by developing and retaining strong staff, clarifying roles and expectations, fostering accountability and professional growth, and aligning personnel and resources with HARC’s strategic priorities. Make difficult organizational decisions when needed while communicating them fairly, respectfully, and transparently.

● **Operations \& infrastructure:** Provide executive oversight of budgets, contracts, compliance, research facilities, farms,

laboratories, and organizational systems; ensure projects meet commitments and deliverables.

● **External relations \& partnership development:** Serve as a visible ambassador for HARC and deepen relationships with Hawaiʻi producers, communities, industry, universities, government agencies, and funders while developing national and international partnerships that advance tropical agricultural research and innovation.

**The Candidate We Seek**

The strongest candidate may come from a nonprofit research institute, agricultural or biotechnology company, university research center, government research organization, agricultural technology company, public\-private partnership, or another science\-based organization. Prior service with the title Executive Director or CEO is valuable but is not required. HARC is interested in demonstrated executive capacity and increasing responsibility.

**Required Qualifications**

● Advanced degree in agriculture, plant science, natural resources, biological sciences, or a closely related field; a PhD or equivalent

advanced scientific training is required.

● Approximately 10 years or more of progressively responsible leadership experience in agriculture, research, biotechnology, natural resources, or another science\-based organization. Exceptional candidates with a demonstrated record of rapidly increasing executive responsibility will be considered.

● Substantial experience leading multidisciplinary scientific, technical, operational, or commercial teams and developing high\-performing staff.

● Demonstrated responsibility for organizational or program budgets, financial planning, grants, contracts, operations, or other significant resources.

● Track record of developing external partnerships and securing or managing diverse sources of funding, such as government grants and contracts, industry\-sponsored research, philanthropy, fee\-for\-service activity, or strategic partnerships.

Resumes without enough detail may not meet the minimum qualification requirements.

When submitting your application via email, be sure to include your full name as well as the job posting name and job posting number in the subject line.

Completed applications should be emailed to: **hr@ptot.texas.gov**

*The agency will contact applicants selected for further consideration. We kindly request that applicants refrain from contacting the agency regarding the status of their applications. Thank you for your interest in employment with our agency.*

**GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of the Executive Council of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Examiners and is responsible for the effective and efficient management and operation of the agency.

The Executive Director provides executive leadership for a 21\-FTE state regulatory agency supporting the Executive Council and two Boards: the Texas Board of Physical Therapy Examiners and the Texas Board of Occupational Therapy Examiners. The position is responsible for implementing the policies, rules, goals, and direction established by the Executive Council and two Boards and for ensuring that agency operations support their statutory responsibilities.

The Executive Director provides leadership and oversight for agency operations, financial management, regulatory administration, workforce management, strategic planning, technology, organizational improvement, compliance, and continuity of operations.

The position requires a hands\-on executive leader who can manage a broad range of agency functions, make sound decisions on complex and sensitive matters, and personally engage in operational issues when necessary.

**REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS**

The Executive Director serves at the discretion of the Executive Council and receives general direction from the Council.

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall management of agency staff and operations and provides executive leadership to the agency's directors, managers, board coordinators, and other employees.

The Executive Council and two Boards are responsible for policymaking and other statutory responsibilities. The Executive Director and agency staff are responsible for management, administration, and implementation of established policies, rules, and direction.

**PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provides overall executive leadership and management of the agency, serving as chief executive officer and ensuring effective and efficient operations consistent with applicable laws, rules, policies, and the direction of the Executive Council and two Boards.
* Advises and supports the Executive Council and two Boards by providing information, recommendations, and administrative support necessary for them to carry out their statutory responsibilities. Maintains clear communication between the governing bodies and agency staff.
* Implements policies, rules, strategic direction, and decisions established by the Executive Council and two Boards, while maintaining the appropriate distinction between policymaking responsibilities and agency management.
* Provides oversight of agency regulatory and administrative operations, including licensing, enforcement, financial, human resources, and other support functions. Personally engages in complex or sensitive operational matters when necessary.
* Provides financial and resource management leadership, including oversight of the agency budget, Legislative Appropriation Request, financial reporting, contracts, expenditures, revenues, and effective allocation of agency resources.
* Leads strategic planning and organizational improvement by establishing priorities, developing operational plans, evaluating agency processes, and implementing improvements that promote efficiency, effectiveness, resilience, and quality service.
* Leads workforce management and development, including recruitment, employee development, performance management, retention, cross\-training, succession planning, knowledge transfer, and organizational structure.
* Leads technology modernization and process improvement efforts, including automation, information security, statewide technology initiatives, and the use of technology to improve agency operations and customer service.
* Ensures compliance with applicable state and federal laws, rules, policies, and regulatory requirements and identifies and addresses legal, operational, financial, and organizational risks.
* Leads emergency preparedness and continuity of operations efforts and ensures the agency is prepared to maintain critical functions during emergencies or other significant disruptions.
* Represents the agency and maintains effective working relationships with state agencies, governmental entities, professional organizations, licensees, stakeholders, and the public.
* Monitors legislative activity affecting the agency and the professions it regulates, prepares or oversees legislative materials and testimony

**Boys \& Girls Clubs of Metro South** is the preeminent youth development organization in Southeastern Massachusetts, serving more than 2,500 youth annually from infancy to adulthood from nearly 50 zip codes at our Clubhouses in Brockton and Taunton, 100\-acre Camp Riverside property, and at several community extension sites across the region. BGCMS is fueled by a critical mission *"to nurture strong minds, healthy bodies and community spirit through youth\-driven, high\-impact programming in safe and fun environments"* to ensure that every child in need of support, opportunity, and belonging has a positive place to spend their out\-of\-school hours. We hold an intrinsic belief that every child deserves an equal chance to pursue the American Dream – to have a genuine opportunity to realize their full potential to achieve a great future.

Reporting to the VP \& Chief Advancement Officer, the **Director of Grants \& Foundation** Relations will lead an established and substantial portfolio of foundation support that is essential to the programs and operations of **Boys \& Girls Clubs of Metro South**. The **Director of Grants \& Foundation Relations** will manage the Club’s Annual Grants Plan, sustaining existing funding partnerships while identifying opportunities to grow foundation support. They will oversee the full lifecycle of foundation grants, from prospect research and relationship cultivation through proposal development, reporting, and stewardship.

The **Director of Grants \& Foundation Relations** will build and strengthen relationships with corporate, community, private, and family foundations, working closely with program, finance, and advancement colleagues to develop compelling requests and communicate the impact of foundation investments. They will also support stewardship initiatives, including funder visits, events, campaigns, impact communications, and special projects.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*This list below includes essential functions that may or may not be assigned to an individual within this role. They are, however, all areas of focus that fall under the umbrella of this position. These duties do not necessarily constitute a full list of responsibilities.*

* Provide leadership in the strategic development of requests for support, including appropriate ask amounts, alignment of foundation funding priorities with the Clubs’ strategic direction, timing of requests, etc.
* Serve as the primary author of all non\-government grant requests to family, community, and corporate foundations with support the Vice President \& Chief Advancement Officer as appropriate.
* Provide secondary support to the Director of Advancement Operations on government grants writing and reporting.
* Manage the Clubs’ Annual Grants Plan through the creation and ongoing maintenance of a comprehensive opportunities/proposals tracking system with the Raiser’s Edge CRM to ensure all requests for support and reports are submitted in accordance with deadlines.
* Support the development and implementation of cultivation and stewardship plans designed to increase partner engagement, community building, and mission investment.
* Research and qualify prospective grant\-making organizations, programs, and opportunities that satisfy the financial needs and goals of the organization and individual programs.
* Utilize database CRM to track and report on the cultivation and stewardship of corporate and family foundation prospects.
* Oversee and manage a portfolio of family and corporate foundation partners, building deep, powerful, and dynamic relationships with current and prospective partners.
* Serve as a representative the organization at external community, foundation, and government events and meetings (ribbon cuttings, networking receptions, etc.) to support prospecting and cultivation efforts.
* Prepare and submit interim and final reports as required by each foundation partner.
* Prepare and submit unrequired interim and final reports for all foundation partners.
* Support the development and distribution of other key mission impact communications (i.e. donor e\-newsletters, Advocacy in Action e\-newsletter, annual reports, etc.) in close collaboration with the Director of Donor Relations and the Director of Marketing \& Communications.
* Attend and contribute to departmental and organizational meetings and events.
* Provide day\-of, on\-site support for our signature annual fundraising and stewardship events, leveraging these gatherings as opportunities to engage with grant funders in attendance.
* Serve as a primary user and administrator of our Raiser’s Edge CRM database, contributing to the overall impact of data through consistent constituent tracking and reporting.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree preferred with at least 4 years of related professional experience.
* Prior experience in a nonprofit development or advancement capacity is strongly preferred, along with knowledge of current and emerging trends in fundraising and grant\-seeking.
* Novice graphic design skills and experience with Canva or similar content creation solution.
* Demonstrated resource management, budgeting, and analytical skills – including the ability to compile and analyze data for planning and reporting purposes.
* Technological proficiency, including a command of the Microsoft Office Suite, and familiarity with using a database to track and extract information.
* Exemplary communication skills (written and verbal) are needed, including the ability to present in front of large groups, interact with and motivate stakeholders, represent the organization at community events and meetings, and write professionally in emails, etc.
* Ability to relate effectively to diverse groups of people (staff, families, youth, etc.) and a track record of building and sustaining meaningful relationships with individuals and teams from all socioeconomic backgrounds.
* Commitment to professionalism including high expectations

jobs.title: Managing Director of Development, Roosevelt Institute
jobs.description:
Working Location:
Hybrid \- New York City or Washington, DC; Approx. 1–2 days onsite/3–4 days offsite  

To apply, please submit a resume, click "Apply Now", and respond to three short\-answer questions in lieu of uploading a cover letter. We must receive your responses to the questions for your application to be reviewed\*.* Please tell us why you are interested in this role and working for the Roosevelt Institute, and how this role aligns with your professional trajectory up to this point (250 words max).
* Walk us through your approach to building and expanding individual giving programs \- how do you develop and cultivate donor relationships? (250 words max)
* This role will manage a four\-person development team \- how do you lead and support staff to foster high\-functioning development teams? (250 words max)

  

Roosevelt’s Work  

The Roosevelt Institute takes on today’s greatest public policy challenges by advancing bold, cutting\-edge research and policy ideas. We believe that the future of the American economy and our democracy depends on a new way of thinking about markets and government—and have successfully engaged with policymakers and the media to inform and shape public debate. Too few people hold too much economic and political power today, and we know that a stronger society is possible if we rectify this imbalance between private actors and the public. With a commitment to restructuring markets, transforming corporations, reviving democratic institutions, and reimagining the role of government, our work moves our nation toward a more resilient, equitable, and green future.  

The Roosevelt Institute is a think tank, a student network, and the nonprofit partner to the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum that, together, are learning from the past and working to redefine our collective future. Focusing on corporate and public power, labor and wages, and the economics of race and gender inequality, the Roosevelt Institute unifies experts, invests in young leaders, and advances progressive policies that bring the legacy of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt into the 21st century.  

What You’ll Do  

Reporting directly to the Chief Development Officer, the Managing Director of Development (MD) will lead fundraising strategy for the Roosevelt Institute’s think tank and people development programs as well as Roosevelt Forward, with a primary focus on building a robust major individual giving program and a secondary focus on providing strategic oversight of institutional/foundation fundraising.  

Roosevelt has strong, long\-standing foundation relationships but has not yet built a dedicated individual giving function, and the organization is in the final stages of rolling out a new strategic plan. This role will leverage that new strategic plan to build an individual giving program largely from the ground up, in service of a three\-to\-five\-year goal of growing individual giving from a portfolio of 5 percent of annual income to 25 percent or close to $5 million annually and diversifying the organization’s revenue base. The MD will partner closely with the Chief Development Officer in shaping the program’s direction and design, will personally cultivate their own portfolio of major individual donors and prospects, and will lead the development team in executing that shared vision.  

Responsibilities include: managing and continuously building a robust pipeline of donors and prospects to support the organization’s work; cultivating and managing relationships with funders; managing the team toward excellent grant writing, project management, and stewardship; partnering with organizational leadership and program staff on new program development and strategy; and other related activities. The MD will oversee a team of four staff: director of foundation relations, donor engagement manager, grants manager, and development associate.  

This is a full\-time, nonunionized, people management role.

Defiance County Economic Development (DCED) is seeking a visionary, collaborative, and results\-driven Executive Director to lead one of Ohio's most successful rural economic development organizations. The Executive Director will be responsible for advancing economic growth, business attraction, business retention and expansion, workforce development partnerships, site development initiatives, housing strategies, and community competitiveness efforts throughout Defiance County.

​

Over the past several years, Defiance County has experienced unprecedented growth, including more than $2\.15 billion in capital investment and nearly 2,000 new jobs announced. **EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

The Alliance Française de Charlottesville (AFC) is seeking an **Executive Director** to lead the organization and oversee its day\-to\-day operations, educational programs, cultural activities, membership, fundraising, and community engagement.

Reporting to the Board of Directors through the Board President, the Executive Director is the organization’s chief staff officer and is responsible for turning the Board’s strategic priorities into effective programs, operations, and measurable results.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead the day\-to\-day operations of AFC in accordance with its mission, bylaws, policies, strategic priorities, and approved budget.
* Develop and implement annual operating plans and priorities established by the Board.
* Monitor organizational performance and provide the Board with regular updates on programs, finances, personnel, and progress toward goals.
* Identify opportunities, challenges, and risks and make recommendations to the Board.

**Educational \& Cultural Programs**

* Oversee AFC’s French\-language classes, instructors, schedules, and educational programming.
* Develop and evaluate classes, conversation groups, cultural events, lectures, and other activities.
* Identify opportunities for new programs and partnerships with educational and cultural organizations.

**Financial \& Administrative Management**

* Work with the Treasurer and Finance Committee to develop the annual budget.
* Monitor income and expenses and ensure operations remain within the approved budget.
* Review financial reports and oversee appropriate financial controls.
* Work with the Treasurer, bookkeeper, accountant, and other professionals on financial reporting, tax filings, and regulatory requirements.
* Authorize routine expenditures within Board\-approved limits.

**Personnel**

* Supervise and evaluate AFC employees and instructors.
* Recruit and oversee instructors in accordance with approved policies and budgets.
* Establish work assignments, expectations, and performance standards.
* Recommend staffing levels and compensation to the Board when appropriate.

**Membership, Fundraising \& Development**

* Develop strategies to attract and retain members and increase participation in AFC programs.
* Cultivate relationships with donors, sponsors, and community partners.
* Identify grant opportunities and coordinate grant applications.
* Develop partnerships that strengthen AFC’s financial sustainability and community presence.

**Community Engagement**

* Serve as a principal public representative of the Alliance Française deCharlottesville.
* Build and maintain relationships with schools, universities, cultural institutions, businesses, community organizations, and Francophone organizations.
* Promote AFC and its programs throughout Charlottesville and the surrounding region.

**Qualifications**

The ideal candidate will have:

* Experience in nonprofit, educational, cultural, or organizational leadership.
* Strong administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
* Experience supervising employees, instructors, or volunteers.
* Familiarity with budgeting and nonprofit financial management.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong commitment to promoting the French language and French and Francophone cultures.
* Knowledge of French and Francophone cultures.
* **French\-language proficiency appropriate to the responsibilities of the position.**

**About the Role**

The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors, staff, instructors, members, volunteers, and community partners to advance AFC’s mission and strengthen its educational and cultural impact in the Charlottesville community.

York Space Systems was founded to radically improve spacecraft affordability and reliability, transforming, and enabling next\- generation space mission operations worldwide. Today, York is one of the most innovative aerospace companies, specializing in end\-to\-end customer solutions and the rapid production of spacecraft platforms. York’s complete Space Segment Solution includes spacecraft production, payload integration, system integration \& test, launch services, ground segment services, and mission operations, enabling customers to leverage York’s existing technology solutions to get to orbit rapidly and responsively. We’re looking to expand our team across the board.
  
  

**Location:** Phoenix, Arizona Metro
  
**Reports to:** CEO \& President, York Space Systems Inc.
  
**Role:** Full\-Time Onsite Senior Leader
  
York Space Systems Inc. seeks a dynamic leader to join us as President and Chief Operating Officer of Solestial LLC, a pioneering solar energy company, which York acquired earlier this year. The position is onsite at Solestial’s headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona. Some travel will be required, primarily to York’s headquarters south of Denver, Colorado, as well as to customer and prospective customer sites.
  
York was founded in 2012 to radically improve spacecraft affordability and reliability. Since that time York has transformed and enabled next generation space mission operations worldwide. Today it is one of the most innovative aerospace companies, specializing in both end\-to\-end customer solutions and the rapid production of spacecraft platforms. York offers a complete space segment solution, including spacecraft production, payload integration, system integration and test, launch services, ground segment services, and mission operations.
  
York seeks an execution\-oriented leader to spearhead Solestial’s next phase of evolution and growth. As the first company to engineer ultra durable, space rated solar solutions designed for mass production, Solestial is redefining the future of solar energy in space. Solestial’s proven, radiation self healing solar technology enhances York’s in\-house portfolio of critical subsystems. As a wholly owned subsidiary of York Inc., Solestial will not only support and supply York, but will continue to supply advanced solar products to external customers. The President and COO will facilitate continued integration with York’s larger portfolio while simultaneously scaling Solestial’s business as a merchant supplier.

* Lead growth, expand market share, build and enhance customer relationships. Strengthen and amplify Solestial’s brand as a premier provider of next generation space solar energy solutions.

* Develop and execute optimal supply chain strategy.
* In coordination with York subject matter experts, guide and execute Solestial’s technology roadmap.

* At least 10 years of experience as a senior executive and leader of teams. The ideal candidate will have proven success in oversight of manufacturing operations and furthering business growth.
* Experience in next generation space, aerospace, energy systems, or high growth deep tech desired.
* Demonstrated accomplishment scaling technology companies from early success to mature organizations.
* Strong understanding of space industry economics, customer ecosystems, procurement cycles, and regulatory frameworks.
* Experience capturing new business and developing and driving partnerships with space agencies and other defense and commercial customers.
* Ability to inspire business development, technical, and operations teams in a mission driven environment.
* Experiencing managing to a P\&L, inclusive of budgeting, top\-line revenue and margin accountability, and support of financial reporting requirements.

jobs.title: Executive Director, QCORE
jobs.description:
The Executive Director of QCORE serves as the head of a university\-wide research institute and works closely with affiliated faculty and staff to build and lead a successful program advancing research and scientific discovery in quantum science, engineering, and business.  

  

QCORE’s primary objective is to empower Montana’s quantum ecosystem by uniting cutting\-edge research, industry partnerships, and community engagement – enabling breakthrough technologies that shape the future of quantum innovation. The vision of QCORE is to lead Montana’s transformation into a global powerhouse for quantum\-enabled technologies by 2035, fostering economic growth, academic excellence and a resilient, future\-focused workforce.  

  

QCORE exists to steward the development of transformative quantum technologies in service to the common good. QCORE will help students plan for careers in quantum and quantum\-enabling systems and will support transitioning into those careers through strategic partnerships with Montana’s growing quantum industry. Strategic partnerships serve as the mechanism for QCORE to strengthen relationships between industry, research and innovators – growing collaboration and creating shared opportunities for beneficial technology innovations.  

  

Pending approval of research center status, QCORE is housed in The College of Letters \& Science (CLS), the largest center for learning, teaching and research at Montana State University. CLS offers students an excellent liberal arts and sciences education in nearly 50 majors, 25 minors and over 25 graduate degrees within the four areas of the humanities, natural sciences, mathematical, and social sciences.  

  

Building on the great strength of our traditional disciplines, the college provides exciting opportunities for faculty and students at the cutting edge of interdisciplinary inquiry. CLS is dedicated to supporting student success, discovering and disseminating new knowledge, and providing an atmosphere in which discovery and learning are integrated and valued. CLS is at the confluence of intellectual tradition, discovery, and innovation.  

  

When research center status is finalized for QCORE, the center will be in the Office of the Vice President for Research and Economic Development.
  

**Duties and Responsibilities**
* Strategically position QCORE to be a nationally recognized, best\-in\-class research and development center for advancement of quantum technology, a leader in quantum workforce development and a deeply integrated innovation ecosystem that supports the translation of quantum and related technologies to industry.
* Develop and implement long\-term strategies to improve QCORE’s overall sustainability, effectiveness, and responsiveness to the needs of sponsoring organizations and companies in the state, region, nation, and internationally.
* Develop and maintain a best\-in\-class governance structure for QCORE.
* Build and nurture long\-term relationships with key stakeholders, including federal agencies, individual donors, institutional funders, congressional representatives, and corporate partners.
* Build strategic alliances and partnerships with other testbeds, academic institutions, corporations, and governments to expand QCORE’s reach, visibility, and impact.
* Lead efforts to secure sustainable funding through partnerships, campaigns, and new initiatives to diversify the organization’s revenue (e.g., federal and private grants, federal cooperative awards, donations, industrial partnerships, social enterprises). This includes engagement with our legislature.
* Participate in sector\-specific organizations relevant to quantum technologies and quantum supply chain, including standards development and testbed communities of practice. Present at national and international gatherings of experts in these respective fields.
* Leads efforts to ensure that QCORE remains a vital part of MSU’s land\-grant mission, promoting quantum science and economic development in Montana, the region, and nation, and providing practical learning opportunities for students.
* Support QCORE faculty and scientists seeking and obtaining external funding to promote innovation, discovery, and dissemination of quantum science and technology.
* Ensure operational excellence, overseeing all aspects of budgeting, accounting, personnel, facilities, security, and safety.
* Ensure that QCORE complies with all legal, regulatory, safety, and ethical standards at local, national, and international levels.
* Ensure that QCORE meets all required grant reporting requirements.
* Coordinate with QCORE’s leadership team to lead and mentor staff, fostering a positive, collaborative, and mission\-driven organizational culture.
* Oversee the monitoring and evaluation of program outcomes to measure success and inform future strategies at a national and international level.
* Prioritize sustainability in all programs and initiatives, ensuring long\-term environmental, social, and financial viability.


  

**Required Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge \& Skills**

**About VMBA**

The Vermont Mountain Bike Association (VMBA) is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit whose mission is to ensure the sustainability of mountain biking in Vermont and thoughtfully promote exceptional riding experiences for all through advocacy, education, and community\-driven stewardship. Founded in 1997, VMBA now counts 28 local Chapters, one central office, and nearly 9,000 individual members. Collectively, our organization deploys more than 25,000\+ volunteer hours to build and maintain over 920 miles of trail. VMBA also serves as the collective voice for mountain biking in Vermont, advocating for policies and legislation that promote more and better trails while also working to cultivate a ridership that knows when, where, and how to ride.

VMBA is guided by our most recent , led by a full\-time Executive Director, and overseen by an active \& engaged Board of Directors.

**Position Summary**

VMBA is currently seeking a self\-direct, results\-driven, and experienced Development Director (DD). In this new position, the DD will work closely with the Executive Director (ED), Fundraising Committee, Board, and staff to build, manage, and mature a robust pipeline of philanthropic supporters, including but not limited to high\-net\-worth individuals, family offices \& foundations, and corporate donors, significantly increasing total annual philanthropic support in order to reach the goals laid out in VMBA’s Strategic Plan. The DD will also work closely with the ED and Marketing \& Communications Manager to design and guide broader public fundraising campaigns, ensuring alignment with VMBA’s strategies to identify and cultivate major individual donors.

This position is full\-time (40 hours per week) with benefits and reports to the Executive Director.

The Development Director’s overarching responsibility is to build and manage a strong pipeline of philanthropic supporters, steward relationships with major donors, and develop the systems and processes to guide the collective VMBA team in donor engagement. Specific responsibilities include:

Additionally, while the Development Director will prepare funding applications to select foundation and family office grant programs, this position is not responsible for broadly seeking and applying for publicly available grant funding.

The New York City Taxi \& Limousine Commission (TLC) oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly one million riders every single day, which is the equivalent of the entire transit system of a medium sized city. The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) is the agency responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for\-hire vehicle industry. With 180,000 licensed drivers and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our city’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for\-hire vehicle sector. TLC continues to be on the front lines of a rapidly changing mobility landscape and our innovative efforts\-whether requiring minimum pay for app drivers, ensuring wheelchair accessible service, making our licensed fleet more environmentally sustainable, working to eliminate traffic fatalities, or preventing discriminatory service\-often serve as a model for other cities.

About Grow Hays

Grow Hays, Inc., a 501(c)(3\) not\-for\-profit organization, is the lead economic development organization for Hays and Ellis County, Kansas. It works to attract new business investment, help existing employers grow, and strengthen the workforce, housing, and infrastructure that growth depends on. Its funding partners include Ellis County, the City of Hays, the City of Ellis, the City of Victoria, and numerous private sector organizations.

Ellis County is a regional hub for northwest Kansas, with anchors in health care, higher education, energy, agriculture, retail, and transportation along I\-70\. Grow Hays partners closely with the City of Hays, Ellis County, Fort Hays State University, Fort Hays Technical College, the Hays Area Chamber of Commerce, Visit Hays, The Bricks, Hays Medical Center, Midwest Energy, and state partners including the Kansas Department of Commerce.

Grow Hays has been the driving force behind the construction of the Grow Hays MicroFactory, the Bob \& Pat Schmidt Community Center, and The Tallgrass and The Grove housing developments. It has also originated more than $3 million in small business loans.

The Director is the main liaison between the Board, the City of Hays, Ellis County, business leaders, education partners, and state and regional agencies. **Department**

College of Business\-Office
**About the University**

  

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.  



Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic\-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first\-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.  



  

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world\-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.  



  

**FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute Vision and Mission**

  

The vision of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute is that MSU Denver students, alumni, faculty, staff, and community partners will have access to the knowledge, resources, experiences, and support they need to understand, enter, and lead within the affordable housing field.  



  

The mission of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute is to advance affordable housing education, workforce development, community engagement, and industry\-connected learning. The Institute prepares students and community members to contribute meaningfully to affordable housing, real estate, finance, policy, development, and community impact through academic programs, non\-credit programming, experiential learning, partnerships, and applied industry engagement.  



  

**Position Summary**

  

The College of Business at MSU Denver seeks a forward\-thinking, visionary, and experienced leader to serve as the next Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute. The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute (AHI) provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and academic integration for MSU Denver’s interdisciplinary affordable housing initiative. This is a 12\-month appointment with ongoing, year\-round administrative and instructional duties reporting to the Dean of the College of Business.  



  

The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute serves as the academic, strategic, and community\-facing leader for affordable housing education, workforce development, industry engagement, non\-credit programming, and interdisciplinary academic integration. Housed within the College of Business but operating with an interdisciplinary and collaborative focus, the Institute supports students, faculty, community partners, housing professionals, developers, financial institutions, nonprofit organizations, public agencies, and industry stakeholders by connecting affordable housing knowledge with education, career pathways, applied learning, and community impact.  



  

The Executive Director is responsible for advancing the Institute’s role as a regional leader in affordable housing education and workforce development. The Executive Director will help position MSU Denver as a distinctive public urban university partner for affordable housing finance, policy, development, management, and community\-centered housing solutions. The Executive Director will also support student success, professional mobility, and industry engagement by helping students and working professionals develop the knowledge, skills, experiences, and relationships needed to contribute to the affordable housing sector. The Executive Director will work closely with faculty, college leadership, college and school partners, University Advancement, C2 Hub, the Affordable Housing Industry Navigator, the AHI Advisory Council, and external stakeholders.  



  

**Responsibilities**

  

Center Executive Director \- Leadership and Strategic Management of the Center (70%)  



  

Strategic Leadership \& Operations


* Provide overall leadership and vision for AHI aligned with the College of Business strategic priorities
* Establish annual goals, program strategy, and operational processes
* Oversee day\-to\-day operations, budgeting, and program execution
Collaborate with the C2 Hub and the AH Industry Navigator to recruit and enroll students into programming  
* 

  

Fundraising \& Advancement


* Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with donors, foundations, and public agencies
* Partner with University Advancement to secure grants, sponsorships, and philanthropic support
Prepare proposals, manage funded projects, and ensure reporting compliance  
* 

  

Community \& Industry Partnerships


* Build and maintain relationships with developers, financial institutions, nonprofits, and government agencies
* Serve as MSU Denver’s representative in housing coalitions and industry forums
Convene events such as summits, panels, and practitioner workshops  
* 

  

Non\-Credit Program Development


* Lead development and promotion of non\-credit programs (certificates, workshops, executive education)
* Recruit instructors and ensure program quality

**The LCMS Mission**

"In grateful response to God's grace and empowered by the Holy Spirit through Word and Sacraments, the mission of The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod is vigorously to make known the love of Christ by word and deed within our churches, communities, and world."


**Department Profile**

The LCMS Board of Directors (BOD) is vested with the general management and supervision of the Synod’s business and legal affairs, including the review and coordination of the policies and directives of the Synod authorized by its Constitution, Bylaws and resolutions and of the plans and policies of the Synod’s boards and commissions. It provides for the administration, financial and operational support, and accountability of the activities of corporate Synod and the oversight and coordination of the same for the broader Synod, as all together pursue the objectives of the Synod as stated in Const. Art. III: to conserve and promote the unity of the true faith, strengthening the witness of Synod members, providing for church worker training and care, for works of mercy, for Christian education, for resourcing of confessional unity, uniformity and variety in responsible practices and customs, ecclesiastical supervision, and protection of congregations and workers in the exercise of their duties and maintenance of their rights.


The Chief Operating Officer of the Synod is an officer of the Synod (Const. Art. XI A) and the board’s executive, serving at the board’s direction in successive three\-year terms as appointed, performing directly or supervising the following functions (Bylaws 3\.4\.1, 3\.4\.1\.3\):


* Administration of the financial affairs of the Synod, excluding the synodwide corporate entities, the districts, the Concordia Plans, and Concordia Plan Services. This includes supervision of all financial\-related areas, including accounts receivable, cash receipts, general and cost accounting, internal audit, budgeting, and corporate insurance. * Administration of the responsibilities given to the Board of Directors in the Constitution, Bylaws, and resolutions of the Synod, now including non\-theological, non\-messaging aspects of communications and fundraising.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
**About the Cotton Charitable Foundation**

The Cotton Charitable Foundation provides families facing a terminal or serious illness with a special place to spend time together, create meaningful memories, and experience moments of joy and connection during an extraordinarily difficult time through Taylor’s Place, a private sanctuary just west of Houston.

Through the generosity of donors, corporate partners, foundations, and event supporters, Taylor’s Place provides families with an opportunity to step away from the challenges of illness and simply be together.

The Cotton Charitable Foundation is entering an exciting period of growth. The organization is seeking a dynamic, relationship\-driven Director of Development to build upon its strong philanthropic foundation, expand its donor base, increase revenue, and create a sustainable development program for the future.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development will lead all aspects of fundraising, development, marketing, and communications for the Cotton Charitable Foundation. This is a hands\-on leadership position for an experienced fundraiser who can develop strategy while actively cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors.

The Director will be responsible for generating revenue through a diversified portfolio of individual giving, major gifts, corporate partnerships, foundation support, special events, and other philanthropic opportunities. In addition to growing philanthropic revenue, the Director will strengthen Taylor’s Place’s visibility and brand through strategic communications, digital engagement, social media, website management, print materials, and compelling storytelling. The Director will ensure that the organization’s external presence effectively communicates its mission, impact, and opportunities for philanthropic support.

A key priority will be growing the organization beyond its existing fundraising model. The Foundation currently hosts one primary fundraising event, and the Director will evaluate and develop additional events and engagement opportunities that generate revenue while introducing new families, donors, corporations, and community partners to the mission.

The ideal candidate will be equally comfortable sitting across the table from a major donor, developing a corporate sponsorship proposal, writing a foundation grant, working with volunteers, and creating a compelling fundraising event.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Development Strategy \& Revenue Growth**

* Develop and implement a comprehensive annual and multi\-year development strategy designed to sustain and grow Taylor’s Place.
* Establish annual fundraising goals, revenue projections, strategies, and measurable performance indicators.
* Develop a diversified fundraising portfolio that reduces reliance on any single source of revenue.
* Identify new sources of philanthropic support and opportunities to expand the organization’s donor base.
* Create and maintain a strong pipeline of prospective donors, corporate partners, foundations, and sponsors.
* Regularly evaluate fundraising results and adjust strategies to maximize opportunities.
* Work closely with the Executive Director to align fundraising priorities with the organization’s strategic vision.

**Major Gifts \& Individual Philanthropy**

* Develop and manage a portfolio of major\-gift prospects and donors.
* Create individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for prospective and current major donors.
* Build relationships with individuals who have the capacity and inclination to make significant investments in Taylor’s Place.
* Partner with Foundation leadership, board members, and key volunteers on donor introductions and solicitations.
* Develop opportunities for donors to make transformational gifts to support Taylor’s Place and its future growth.
* Strengthen annual giving and identify opportunities to move annual donors into higher levels of engagement and philanthropy.

**Corporate \& Foundation Relations**

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate partners and sponsors.
* Develop meaningful partnerships with businesses that align with Taylor’s Place’s mission and values.
* Create compelling sponsorship opportunities that provide meaningful engagement and visibility for corporate partners.
* Research and pursue foundation funding opportunities aligned with Taylor’s Place programs and priorities.
* Oversee grant proposals, letters of inquiry, reports, renewals, and funder communications.
* Develop long\-term relationships with corporate and foundation partners rather than focusing solely on individual funding requests.

**Events \& Special Events Growth**

Taylor’s Place currently has one established fundraising event. A major responsibility of this position will be to thoughtfully expand the organization’s event strategy.

* Provide strategic leadership for the existing fundraising event, maximizing revenue, sponsorships, attendance, and donor engagement.
* Evaluate the feasibility and potential return on investment of additional fundraising events.
* Develop and implement new events and fundraising experiences that introduce Taylor’s Place to new audiences.
* Develop event sponsorship opportunities and secure corporate and individual support.
* Recruit and engage event committees, volunteers, community leaders, and ambassadors.
* Ensure events serve not only as fundraising opportunities but also as vehicles for donor cultivation, community awareness, and long\-term relationship building.
* Establish financial and performance metrics for each event and evaluate results annually.

**Donor Stewardship \& Engagement**

* Create a comprehensive donor stewardship program that ensures supporters understand the impact of their generosity.
* Develop personalized communications and engagement strategies for key donors.
* Ensure timely acknowledgments, impact reports, invitations, updates, and other donor communications.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description  

  

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world\-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.


**Why join the Harvard Kennedy School?**


The John F. Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University is one of 12 graduate and professional schools at the university. Harvard Kennedy School’s mission is to improve public policy and leadership so people can live in societies that are more safe, free, just, and sustainably prosperous. By combining cutting\-edge research, the teaching of outstanding students, and direct interaction with practitioners, we have an impact on solving public problems that no other institution can match. When you work at Harvard Kennedy School, you make a difference.

  

  

Job Description  

  

Harvard Kennedy School Executive Education (HKS Exec Ed) is the premier worldwide source for executive\-level leadership development focused on public service. Exec Ed operates as a department within HKS and provides 80\+ programs ranging from 1 to 4 weeks in length to 4500\+ participants each year. Programs are delivered online, in\-person, or a combination of both, and are offered as open enrollment via an admissions process or as custom programs focused on the needs of public service or government organizations, sponsors, or donors. Exec Ed is a critical piece of the HKS mission to improve public policy and leadership so people can live in societies that are more safe, free, just, and sustainably prosperous. Programs are led by faculty and attract accomplished public leaders from around the world, with roles in the government, nonprofit, multilateral, and corporate sectors.


Harvard Kennedy School (HKS) seeks a Program Director to join our Executive Education team. Reporting to the Senior Director, Program Management, the Program Director manages an assigned portfolio of 6\-8 executive education programs with budget responsibilities of approx. $3M. Programs include both new and existing. The Program Director is responsible for leading all aspects of assigned programs, including coordinating faculty effort, ensuring participant satisfaction, managing operational staff, grant/gift submission and reporting as needed and achieving financial targets, to ensure that Executive Education programs are delivered with excellence. We seek collaborative, adaptable candidates who love the details of programs and events, are driven by working with others on a fast\-paced team and are excited about having an impact on our world by supporting leaders from around the country and the world. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive team culture and seek candidates who share our values and commitment.

  

  

**Job\-Specific Responsibilities:**

As a Program Director, you will represent HKS, Executive Education to faculty and program participants in your portfolio of programs as well as external partners/vendors. In this capacity, you will manage:


PROGRAM MANAGEMENT


* Manage all aspects of admissions and enrollment process, including admission decisions and fellowship/tuition assistance award decisions.
* Review, enhance and implement existing marketing and outreach strategies, in coordination with the Executive Education marketing team and Senior Director. Strategy may include direct mail, conference participation, third party funding relationships, recruiting meetings, and/or sales visits to target groups.
* Key contributor during the launch process of new programming.
* Manages communication strategy and processes with prospective participants.
* Organize reports and data for faculty chair(s) and Senior Director of program management.

PROGRAM DELIVERY


* Lead a delivery team in 6\-8 new and existing programs, ensuring all aspects of program development and implementation are planned, managed, and executed at the highest standards.
* Direct each program’s operations, including all aspects of logistics, faculty relationships, curriculum management, and coordination with custom clients, as needed.
* Develop strong working relationships with faculty chair; staff faculty chair for program activity as appropriate; Consulting with faculty chair on major program related activity and/or decisions as needed. Responsible for informing faculty chair about standards within EE, such as faculty comp guidelines and the process related to the hiring of teaching assistants.
* Negotiate with new and existing external vendors, sign contracts on behalf of the program for offsite events.
* Take the lead in anticipating and resolving issues and escalating to the senior director as needed.
* Manage processes to ensure program participants are supported before, during and after the programs, online and in person.
* Act as project manager for new and existing programming.
* Review program evaluations with faculty chair(s) to determine and implement changes in program content for future offerings.

OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP


* Exercise financial management and oversight of assigned programs, including budgeting, faculty compensation and fulfilling all required reporting processes, including financial reconciliation and the Program Review \& Outlook (PRO) process. Track and comply with any external reporting requirements; for example, with third party payers.
* Responsible for grant/gift submissions and reporting.
* Seek opportunities to develop and lead improvements to standard operating procedures across all programs.

TEAM MANAGEMENT
